statement: The band and its canonical decompositions: Put \[ \Gamma=W(p)=\{\lambda\in\overline\Q^{\times}:\ p^N\lambda\text{ is integral for some }N\geq0, \quad |\tau\lambda|=p^{w(\lambda)/2}\ (\tau),\quad w(\lambda)\in\Z\}. \] Then $G=D(\Gamma)$, where $D$ is the contravariant equivalence from Galois modules to groups of multiplicative type. Let $\mu_\infty$ be the group of roots of unity, $\Gamma^0=\ker(w)$, and $M=\Gamma^0/\mu_\infty$. There are canonical identifications \begin{align*} X^*(G^0)&=\Gamma/\mu_\infty=M\oplus\Z[\sqrt p],\\ G/G^0&=\widehat\Z,\qquad G^0=H^0\times\Gm, \qquad H^0=D(M),\\ X^*(H)&=\Gamma'=\Gamma/\langle\mu_\infty,p\rangle =M\oplus\Z/2\Z,\\ H&=H^0\times\mu_2. \end{align*} The maps $\epsilon:G\to\Gm$ and $i:\Gm\to G$ have character maps $1\mapsto p$ and $\lambda\mapsto w(\lambda)$, respectively, and $\epsilon i(t)=t^2$. The restriction $i|_{\mu_2}$ splits $H$. The group $M$ is a $\Q$-vector space, and complex conjugation acts as $-1$. Consequently $H^0$ is a protorus, an inverse limit of tori compact at the real place. It is not an algebraic torus of finite type.
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the group calculation is unconditional
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The transcription is not a group definition: The transcription of 15:5 reads ``entiers alg\'ebriques'' and ``$\nu\in\mathbf Z^+$''. Those elements form a monoid, not the character group of a rigid category: $p$ is in it and $p^{-1}$ is not. We have explicitly replaced that text by its group of fractions. Both positive and negative integral weights occur. Weight zero does not imply root of unity once denominators at $p$ are allowed. Also the arrow transcribed as $i|_{\mu_2}:\mu_2\to H^0$ must land in $H$; its composite with $H\to\mu_2$ is the identity, so it cannot land in $H^0$.
status: Refuted literally; corrected by Theorem~\ref{A:band}
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Artin versus Artin--Tate rigidification: Let $F^0$ be the intrinsic fibre functor on $\operatorname{Niv}^0(\mathcal M)^0$, the Artin motives. The gerbe of fibre functors extending this $F^0$, with an identification on that subcategory, has band $G^0$, not $H$. To obtain band $H$ one must also fix a trivialization of the Tate line. Equivalently one extends $F^0$ to the Artin--Tate subcategory by $F^0(\Q(1))=\Q$. Its group is \[ G/H=D(\mu_\infty\oplus\Z p) =\widehat\Z\times\Gm. \]
status: Refuted as literally formulated in the prompt; corrected statement proved
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Geometric base change and the universal Frobenius: There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \Gamma/\mu_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim} W(p^\infty):=\varinjlim_{n\mid n'} \bigl(W(p^n),\lambda\mapsto\lambda^{n'/n}\bigr). \] Thus $G^0=P$, the Weil-number protorus of Langlands--Rapoport and Milne, and $H^0=P_0$, its weight-zero factor. The base-change functor $\mathcal M_p\to\mathcal M_{\overline{\F}_p}$ induces the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow G$ on bands. The inclusion $\Gamma\hookrightarrow\overline\Q^\times$ is Galois equivariant and hence defines a canonical $\mathfrak f\in G(\Q)$.
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; identification of character modules unconditional
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Centres and crystalline endomorphisms: For a simple $N\in\mathcal M_q$ the algebra $A_N=\End(N)$ is a central division algebra over $E_N=\Q[\mathfrak f_N]$, and \[ A_N\otimes\Q_p\simeq \End_{F\text{-}\mathrm{Isoc}(\F_q)}(T_pN). \] The right side means endomorphisms commuting with crystalline Frobenius, including its semilinear structure. It does not mean all endomorphisms of the underlying vector space. If $d_N^2=[A_N:E_N]$, then $\operatorname{rank}(N)=d_N[E_N:\Q]$.
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The warning about $\Z$ and $\widehat\Z$: Over $\F_p$, an isocrystal is a finite-dimensional $\Q_p$-vector space with an invertible \emph{linear} operator. Forgetting the operator is an exact faithful tensor functor to $\Q_p$-vector spaces. Thus $T_p$, after this forgetting, really is a fibre functor over $\Q_p$. Its Frobenius action generally does not extend continuously from $\Z$ to $\widehat\Z$. Over $\overline{\F}_p$ the realization instead takes values in the $\Q_p$-linear category $\mathcal R_p$ of isocrystals on $B=W(\overline{\F}_p)[1/p]$. Its fibre-functor gerbe has band $D(\Q)$ and class $\beta_p$ characterized by \[ \operatorname{inv}_p\bigl(s_*(\beta_p)\bigr)=s\pmod\Z, \qquad s\in\Q=X^*(D(\Q)). \] It is not neutral over $\Q_p$.
status: Proved; Lead A2 is false in its proposed nonneutral interpretation over $\F_p$
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The Artin torsor and the connecting map: For the Artin--Tate rigidification of Proposition~\ref{A:rigidification}, let $\eta_p=\operatorname{Isom}^{\otimes}(T_p|_{\mathrm{Artin}},F^0_p)$, with the right action on the source; extend it by the trivial Tate factor. Under \[ H^1(\Q_p,G/H)=H^1(\Q_p,\widehat\Z) =\Hom_{\rm cts}(G_{\Q_p},\widehat\Z), \] it is the unramified quotient. Arithmetic local Frobenius maps to $+1$ when the canonical motivic Frobenius is the generator $+1$. The opposite isomorphism torsor has value $-1$ and gives $\xi_p=-\partial(\eta_p^{\mathrm{op}})$ instead. The class of the rigidified gerbe is \[ \xi_p=\partial(\eta_p),\qquad \partial:H^1(\Q_p,G/H)\longrightarrow H^2(\Q_p,H). \]
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the Artin calculation is unconditional
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The real obstruction, with the Serre argument repaired: The full category over $\F_p$ has no $\R$-valued fibre functor. At infinity the rigidified gerbe has class \[ \xi_\infty=(0,1/2)\in H^2(\R,H^0)\times H^2(\R,\mu_2)=0\times\Z/2\Z. \] The nonzero class is represented by the real Weil extension, whose lift $j$ of complex conjugation satisfies $j^2=-1$.
status: Proved for abelian motives, and hence under the stated hypothesis for all motives
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Compact real tori satisfy the degree-two Hasse principle: If $T/\Q$ is a torus compact over $\R$, with character lattice $L$, then $\Sha^2(\Q,T)=0$. In fact \[ H^2(\Q,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T). \]
status: Proved unconditionally
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The global class really is locally determined: For $H^0=D(M)$ one has \[ \Sha^2(\Q,H^0)=0,\qquad H^2(\R,H^0)=0. \] For a finite place $v$, there is a canonical identification \[ H^2(\Q_v,H^0)=\Hom\bigl(M^{G_{\Q_v}},\Q/\Z\bigr). \] More precisely, for any cofinal countable increasing sequence of Galois-stable lattices $L_n\subset M$, and $T_n=D(L_n)$, \[ H^2(\Q,H^0)=\varprojlim_n H^2(\Q,T_n) =\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T_n). \] These equalities are conclusions of the proof, not definitions of cohomology. The assertion in A.3 that $\Sha^2$ of an arbitrary protorus is simply a limit of finite-level $\Sha^2$ is not a valid general rule.
status: Proved unconditionally for the band in Theorem~\ref{A:band}
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Explicit global and local classes: Write $v_p(p)=1$, and for $m\in M$ choose a Weil-unit representative $u$. The number $v_p(m):=v_p(u)$ is independent of that choice. There is exactly one class \[ \xi_0=(a_p,b_{p,\infty})\in H^2(\Q,H^0)\times H^2(\Q,\mu_2) \] with local components \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{lll} \toprule Place & $H^0$ component & $\mu_2$ component\\ \midrule $\ell\ne p,\infty$ & $0$ & $0$\\ $p$ & $m\mapsto v_p(m)\pmod\Z$, $m\in M^{G_{\Q_p}}$ & $1/2$\\ $\infty$ & $0$ & $1/2$\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} Here $b_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion Brauer class ramified exactly at $p$ and infinity, viewed in $H^2(\Q,\mu_2)$ by Kummer. The compact component $a_p$ has infinite order. The finite local components determine both factors of $\xi_0$.
status: Proved unconditionally for the constructed gerbe; motivic identification under the stated hypotheses
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An explicit arithmetic description of the character module: For finite Galois CM fields $K\subset\overline\Q$, let $X_K$ be their sets of primes above $p$. Then \[ M\simeq\varinjlim_K \{f:X_K\to\Q:\ f(cw)=-f(w)\}, \] where transition maps pull back functions along maps of primes, and $[u]$ maps to $w\mapsto\operatorname{ord}_w(u)/ \operatorname{ord}_w(p)$. In particular the local groups and the functional in Theorem~\ref{A:class} are specified by explicit rational permutation modules.
status: Proved unconditionally
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The correct comparison, and the strict-band counterexample: Let $\mathscr H$ be the Artin--Tate rigidified gerbe of class $\xi_0$. Its pushout along $H\hookrightarrow P=G^0$ is the pseudomotivic $P$-gerbe of \citet[Theorem 3.29 and Theorem 3.31]{AMilne1994}, with the inverse-limit and adelic corrections of \citet[Theorem 6.3 and Definition 6.6]{AMilne2003}. Equivalently it is the gerbe obtained by rigidifying only the Artin fibre functor $F^0$, and under the motivic hypotheses it is the gerbe of motives over $\overline{\F}_p$. There is no band-preserving equivalence of the $H$-gerbe itself or of the full $G$-gerbe with that $P$-gerbe. Their bands have component groups $\mu_2$, $\widehat\Z$, and $1$, respectively. The morphisms that do exist are pushouts \[ \mathscr H\longrightarrow\mathscr P \longrightarrow\mathscr G, \qquad H\hookrightarrow P\hookrightarrow G. \]
status: Strict equivalence with band $H$ or $G$ refuted; corrected equivalence proved under the stated hypotheses
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Dictionary between gerbes and groupoids: Let $\mathscr P$ be a $P$-gerbe over $\Q$ and choose $x\in\mathscr P(\overline\Q)$. Its groupoid over $\Spec(\overline\Q)\times_{\Spec\Q}\Spec(\overline\Q)$ is the sheaf of isomorphisms between the two pullbacks of $x$. Its diagonal kernel is $P_{\overline\Q}$. For each place $v$, a realization functor induces a morphism of such groupoids; its map on kernels is $1\to P_{\Q_\ell}$ for $\ell\ne p$, $D(\Q)\to P_{\Q_p}$ at $p$, and $\Gm\to P_\R$ at infinity. Conversely fpqc descent for this groupoid recovers $\mathscr P$. Changing $x$ changes the groupoid by an isomorphism whose conjugacy ambiguity is exactly the change of the chosen identification of objects.
status: Proved
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Unconditional $H$-gerbe and its automorphisms: The class in Theorem~\ref{A:class} defines an $H$-gerbe over $\Q$ with exactly the prescribed local classes. It is unique up to $H$-equivalence. No nonzero class can be added without changing some local class. The group of isomorphism classes of its band-preserving self-equivalences is \[ H^1(\Q,H)=\Q^\times/\Q^{\times2}\times \frac{\prod_n T_n(\Q)} {\{(a_n f_n(a_{n+1})^{-1})_n:(a_n)_n\in\prod_nT_n(\Q)\}}, \] for the explicit lattice exhaustion in Theorem~\ref{A:hasse}; $f_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is its transition. The group of automorphisms of any one such equivalence is $H(\Q)=\{\pm1\}$.
status: Proved unconditionally as a statement about banded gerbes
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The bare category and the category with local data: Fix the band diagram $H\hookrightarrow G$, the grading $i$, and the augmentation $\varepsilon$, with the Artin--Tate rigidification specified in Proposition~\ref{A:rigidification}. Then $\xi_0$ determines the underlying Tannakian category with these structures up to compatible equivalence, and conversely. It does not in general determine a family of chosen local neutralizations extending the fixed rigidification. Write $S=\{\ell:\ell\ne p,\ \ell\text{ finite}\}$. The precise replacement for that stronger classification is relative cohomology, defined by the shifted cone of $R\Gamma(\Q,H)\to\prod_{\ell\in S}R\Gamma(\Q_\ell,H)$. For a fixed locally trivializable class its fibre is a torsor under \[ \coker\left[H^1(\Q,H)\longrightarrow \prod_{\ell\in S}H^1(\Q_\ell,H)\right]. \] The same statement with a restricted adelic product applies when an integral compatibility condition is imposed.
status: Bare classification proved; classification of arbitrary framed local data by the bare class refuted
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Forgetting the local comparison framings: Fix the category and global Artin--Tate rigidification of Proposition~\ref{A:enrichment}. Suppose that the prime-to-$p$ realizations form one object over the finite adeles away from $p$, and that this adelic object's Artin restriction is isomorphic to $F^0\otimes\mathbb A_f^p$, not just separately at each place. At $p$ fix the Artin restriction of the ordinary crystalline $\Q_p$ fibre functor, namely the unramified Artin torsor computed in Proposition~\ref{A:eta}. If the local comparison isomorphisms with these restrictions are \emph{not} part of the data, all such coherent systems on the fixed gerbe are equivalent. One may also include the prescribed real realization morphism. Thus the underlying class suffices for the equivalence class of this unframed coherent system. This assertion and the framed counterexample in Proposition~\ref{A:enrichment} concern different specified data. The equivalence itself is not asserted to be unique as an equivalence preserving the global $H$-rigidification.
status: Proved for coherent adelic systems with the prescribed Artin restrictions
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: What the Lefschetz category actually supplies: Let $\operatorname{LMot}(\overline{\F}_p)$ be the category generated by abelian varieties, with correspondences generated by divisor classes and with the ordinary Tannakian commutativity constraint. It is a semisimple Tannakian category. Its band is \[ L=\mathop{\prod}_{\Pi}^{\Gm} L_\Pi,\qquad X^*(L_\Pi)=\Z^{\Pi}/ \{f:c f=f,\ \textstyle\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}f(\pi)=0\}, \] where $\Pi$ runs through the geometric simple isogeny classes, identified with Galois orbits of integral weight-one Weil germs. The fibre product identifies every multiplier $[\pi]+[c\pi]$. In particular $L$ is commutative, but it is not the Weil-number protorus $P$ in general. Compatible powers of Frobenius generate a subgroup $P\hookrightarrow L$. Prime-to-$p$ realization and crystalline realization, the weight and Tate morphisms, and the real obstruction are available unconditionally. The claimed identification of the entire character group with Weil numbers, full Frobenius-centralizer faithfulness for arbitrary tensor objects, and the resulting formula for $H^0$ cannot simply be transferred to this smaller-correspondence category.
status: Proved unconditionally; equality of its band with $P$ is refuted
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An explicit extra Frobenius relation: Take $p=5$, $\alpha=1+2i$, and $\beta=(3+\sqrt{-11})/2$. They are Frobenius numbers of the elliptic curves \[ E_\alpha:y^2=x^3+x,\qquad E_\beta:y^2=x^3+4x+2 \quad\text{over }\F_5, \] which have four and three rational points, respectively. Choose $\lambda^2=\alpha\beta$. This is an integral weight-one $5$-Weil number, with irreducible polynomial \[ x^8-6x^6+15x^4-150x^2+625. \] Honda--Tate supplies a simple abelian fourfold $B/\F_5$ with this Frobenius number. In \[ h^1(B)^{\otimes2}\otimes h^1(E_\alpha)^\vee \otimes h^1(E_\beta)^\vee \] there is a geometric eigenline on which Frobenius is $1$, but the Lefschetz group acts nontrivially. Thus its character is zero on $P$ and nonzero on $L$.
status: Refuted: $L=P$ for all finite-field Lefschetz motives
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The unconditional gerbes used in Kisin's paper: Kisin's quasi-motivic gerbe has a band $Q$ defined by a universal condition on real and $p$-adic cocharacters. Its pushout by $Q\twoheadrightarrow P$ is the pseudomotivic gerbe, with the same $P$ and the same local realization morphisms as above. This construction is unconditional. It supplies a Tannakian category of representations of that gerbe; identifying that category with all numerical motives is a separate claim with the hypotheses of A.1. The quasi-motivic band $Q$ itself is not a replacement name for $G$, $H$, or $P$.
status: Known construction; the signed dictionary proved and independently checked
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The literature date changes the abelian scope: The dated primary preprint of \citet[Theorem I]{AvanHoftenSempliner2026} proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Its \S1.1.2--1.1.3 applies Milne's Hodge-to-Tate implication to all abelian varieties over finite fields. With these cited results the full-correspondence category of abelian motives, and all its tensor powers, has the Weil band $P$ unconditionally. This does not change the Lefschetz category: the latter was defined by restricting its morphisms to those generated by divisors, and Example~\ref{A:lefschetz-counterexample} still proves that its band can be larger. Nor does this theorem settle the Tate conjecture for arbitrary smooth projective varieties. The preprint status and exact version are retained in the bibliography rather than represented as an earlier theorem.
status: Known from the opened October 2026 theorem; the implication is stated explicitly
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Restriction on the arithmetic class: For \(k_m=\F_{q^m}\), restriction sends \[ e_q\longmapsto m e_{q^m}. \] For the point, Weil--etale motivic cohomology is \[ H^i_{\BW}(\Spec\F_q,\Z(n))= \begin{cases} \Z,&n=0,\ i=0,1,\\ \Z/(q^{|n|}-1),&n\ne0,\ i=1,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases}\tag{B.1} \] where for negative twists the etale convention is \(\Z(n)=\Q/\Z'(n)[-1]\), with the characteristic-primary part omitted. After tensoring with \(\Q\), only the two groups with \(n=0\) survive.
status: Proved
notes: Negative twists use Q/Z prime-to-characteristic shifted by -1; l=p cyclotomic convention excluded.

statement: The precise comparison gate: Let \(X/\F_q\) be smooth and projective of dimension \(d\). In the notation of Geisser's Conjectures~8.1--8.3, let \(K(X,n)\) denote the integral Weil--etale to continuous-cohomology comparison, \(L(X,n)\) finite generation, and \(T(X,n)\) the conjunction of the Tate cycle-class conjecture in codimension \(n\), semisimplicity at eigenvalue one, and equality of rational and numerical equivalence in that codimension. Then \[ K(X,n)+K(X,d-n)\ \Longrightarrow\ L(X,n) \ \Longrightarrow\ K(X,n)\ \Longrightarrow\ T(X,n). \tag{B.2} \] Assuming \(T(Y,r)\) for every smooth projective variety over finite fields and every \(r\), all the comparisons \(K(X,n)\) and finite-generation statements \(L(X,n)\) follow. Moreover, independently of these conjectures, \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Q(n))\simeq H^i_{\BM}(X,\Q(n))\oplus H^{i-1}_{\BM}(X,\Q(n)). \tag{B.3} \] Cup product with \(e_q\) acts on these summands by \( (a,b)\mapsto(0,a)\).
status: Proved
notes: The literal continuity and algebraically closed vanishing requirements contradict the finite-point computation. The compatible universal comparison reduces, under Tate and semisimplicity, to cycle injectivity only in codimension m on varieties of dimension2m-1, m>=2, equivalently to numerical Chow phantom vanishing. All abelian-type cases are proved using the current external CM Hodge theorem.; Universal three-part Geisser T implies comparison and finite generation.

statement: A contradiction already at the point: There is no cohomology theory which simultaneously has the finite-field Weil--etale value \(H^1(\F_q,\Q)=\Q e_q\), the restriction in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-e}, continuity under the filtered union of finite extensions, and vanishing of higher cohomology over \(\overline{\F}_q\).
status: Refuted; corrected statement proved
notes: The direct limit of the degree-one rational lines is Q, not zero.

statement: All twists for motives of abelian type, using the current theorem: Let \(X/\F_q\) be smooth projective, and suppose that its rational Chow motive belongs to the thick rigid category generated by abelian varieties and Artin motives. Then, for every \(i,n\) and every prime \(\ell\), \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Z(n))\otimes\Z_\ell \xrightarrow{\sim}H^i_{\Bcts}(X,\Z_\ell(n)), \] and all the integral Weil--etale groups are finitely generated. For \(\ell=p\), the right side is the logarithmic Hodge--Witt comparison, rather than a cyclotomic etale sheaf in characteristic \(p\). In particular, \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Q(n))= \begin{cases} CH^n(X)_\Q,&i=2n,\ 2n+1,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \] where cup product by the normalized \(e_q\) identifies the two copies. Thus the previously known divisor and curve cases extend to all twists on all abelian varieties, and on all varieties of abelian type. This statement does not assert that every Chow motive is of abelian type.
status: Proved from the cited current theorem
notes: Current CM Hodge theorem implies all-abelian Tate. Tate passes to abelian-type projectors; Kimura nilpotence supplies rational=numerical, so every integral comparison and finite generation follow, including logarithmic p-adic coefficients.

statement: The remaining universal assertion is exactly a phantom-motive gate: Assume Tate surjectivity and semisimplicity at eigenvalue one for every smooth projective variety over \(\F_q\), in every codimension. Then the following universal statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The integral Weil--etale comparison holds for all varieties, degrees and twists, and all these integral groups are finitely generated. \item Rational equivalence equals numerical equivalence on all rational Chow groups. \item There is no nonzero rational Chow motive \(P\) whose image \(\bar P\) in numerical motives is zero. \item Every rational Chow motive belongs to the category generated by abelian and Artin motives. \end{enumerate} In particular, the missing assertion in B.1 can be expressed without an unspecified regulator or unspecified comparison map: it is the vanishing of numerical Chow phantoms. The Tate and semisimplicity hypotheses alone have not been shown to imply that vanishing here.
status: Proved equivalence; the equivalent universal assertion remains unresolved
notes: Explicit splitting M=N+P with N abelian-type and P numerical phantom; nilpotence on N corrects the lifted inverse. This is an exact remaining obstruction, not a proof phantoms vanish.

statement: A smaller index set for the remaining Chow comparison: Keep the universal Tate and eigenvalue-one semisimplicity hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:B-phantom-gate}. Fix \(\ell\ne p\). The universal comparison in that proposition is equivalent to injectivity of the cycle map only for the pairs \[ \dim X=2m-1,\qquad \operatorname{CH}^{m}(X)_\Q\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^{2m}(\bar X,\Q_\ell(m)), \qquad m\ge2. \tag{B.9a} \] Here all smooth projective varieties in the displayed dimensions, over all finite extensions under consideration, are quantified. There is also a dimension-preserving version: to obtain Beilinson's injectivity in every codimension for varieties of dimension at most \(D\), it suffices to prove it for \[ 3\le d\le D,\qquad 2\le i\le\lceil d/2\rceil. \tag{B.9b} \] The first still undecided ordinary-Chow assertion in either range is codimension two on threefolds. Under the fixed Tate hypotheses, that assertion is equivalent to \[ H^4(F_0\mathbb P^4_{\overline{\F}_q},\Q_\ell(3))^ {\Gal(\overline{\F}_q/\F_q)}=0, \tag{B.9c} \] where \(H^a(F_0Y,\Q_\ell(b))\) means the colimit of continuous \(\ell\)-adic cohomology over dense open subsets of \(Y\). It is not defined by tensoring the Milnor \(K\)-group of the function field with \(\Q_\ell\).
status: Proved reduction; the restricted cycle-injectivity assertion remains unresolved
notes: Under universal Tate and semisimplicity, half-codimension Beilinson suffices in each dimension bound; product with P^(d-2i+1) then reduces the universal test to one codimension in each odd dimension. First new case is codimension2 threefolds, not a proof that this case alone implies all higher cases.

statement: Rational varieties as a restricted test class: Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate}, the remaining universal comparison is equivalent to cycle-class injectivity only for \[ \operatorname{CH}^{2m}(Y)_\Q\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^{4m}(\bar Y,\Q_\ell(2m)), \qquad \dim Y=4m-1,\quad m\ge2, \] where \(Y\) ranges over smooth projective rational varieties over all the finite constant-field extensions under consideration. It even suffices to test the varieties obtained by blowing up \(\mathbb P^{4m-1}\) along a smooth projective centre of dimension \(2m-1\). In particular, the codimension-two threefold problem embeds as a split summand of the codimension-four problem on rational sevenfolds. This does not reduce it to rational threefolds.
status: Proved test-class reduction; the same Chow obstruction remains
notes: Explicit exceptional maps I_m=j_*(xi^(m-1)pi^*) and R_m=-pi_*(xi^(m-1)j^*) compose to identity. First threefold CH2 case embeds in rational sevenfold CH4, not rational threefolds. Encoding arbitrary centres is not counted as new gate movement.

statement: A surface-support criterion for the first Chow gate: Let \(X/k\) be smooth, projective and geometrically integral, where \(k\) is finite, and put \(n=\dim X\geq2\). Suppose that, after a finite extension of \(k\), there is a closed subscheme \(S\subset X\), of dimension at most two, for which \[ [\eta_X]\in\operatorname{im}\bigl( CH_0(S_{k(X)})_{\Q}\longrightarrow CH_0(X_{k(X)})_{\Q}\bigr). \tag{B.S1} \] Then rational and numerical equivalence agree on codimension-two cycles on \(X\). In particular, for every \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\), \[ CH^2(X)_{\Q}\otimes_{\Q}\Q_\ell\longrightarrow H^4(X_{\overline k},\Q_\ell(2)) \quad\hbox{is injective}. \] Condition~\eqref{eq:B-generic-surface-support} is equivalent to universal rational support on this fixed \(S\): the pushforward \(CH_0(S_L)_{\Q}\to CH_0(X_L)_{\Q}\) is surjective for every field extension \(L/k\). Thus it is a condition over function fields, not merely a condition on zero-cycles over the finite base field. For threefolds satisfying it, rational and numerical equivalence agree in every ordinary Chow degree.
status: Proved; the unrestricted threefold gate remains unresolved
notes: Exact generic-point criterion is equivalent to universal fixed-surface support over every field extension. Transposed diagonal factors CH2 through CH2 of a smooth surface and Pic of a smooth divisor alteration; both numerically trivial parts are rationally zero over finite fields. No individual Parshin or full Weil comparison inferred. Movement classification left to formal review; not automatically counted as a new universal-gate reduction.

statement: Geometrically uniruled threefolds: Every smooth projective geometrically uniruled threefold over a finite field satisfies rational equals numerical equivalence in every ordinary Chow degree. In particular the first unresolved codimension-two threefold test in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate} may be restricted to threefolds which are not geometrically uniruled.
status: Proved ordinary Chow equality; no full motivic comparison inferred
notes: A generically finite rational map T timesP1 toX moves the generic point to the image of T timesa after finite extension, even for inseparable generic degree. Thus the first codimension-two threefold test can exclude geometrically uniruled varieties; no automatic claim of gate movement or of full higher-motivic comparison.

statement: Two failures of interchange in a proposed symbol proof: The following two implications, which might otherwise be used to attack Proposition~\ref{prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate}, are false. \begin{enumerate} \item Put \(k=\overline{\F}_2\), \(L=k(t)\), and \(\ell=3\). The natural map \[ \varinjlim_{U\subset\mathbf P^1_k} H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(U,\Z_3(1)) \longrightarrow H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Spec L,\Z_3(1)), \] where \(U\) runs over dense opens, is injective and not surjective. It remains nonsurjective after tensoring with \(\Q_3\), and an explicit omitted class is invariant under \(\Gal(k/\F_2)\). \item There is a torsion-free \(\Z\)-module \(M\) with an automorphism \(F\), such that every element of \(M\otimes\Q\) has finite \(F\)-orbit, but the rationalized \(3\)-adic completion has a nonzero \(4\)-eigenvector. Thus local finiteness before completion does not exclude a non-root-of-unity eigenvalue after completion. \end{enumerate}
status: Proved counterexamples to two limit arguments; the B1 gate is unchanged.
notes: An invariant infinite-support Kummer class lies in continuous field H1 but outside the open colimit, even rationally. A locally finite Frobenius module gains a non-torsion4-eigenvector after3-adic completion. The distinct direct-sum fixed-orbit permutation calculation remains valid. Neither diagnostic is a counterexample to a cycle conjecture.

statement: The Chow obstruction on an explicit fixed open: Let \(k=\F_q\), let \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\), and put \(Y=\mathbb P^4_k\). Let \(D_1,D_2\subset Y\) be smooth hypersurfaces of positive degree meeting transversely in a smooth surface \(S\). Write \(U=Y\setminus(D_1\cup D_2)\) and \(\Gamma=\Gal(\bar k/k)\). Assume the divisor Tate conjecture for \(S\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} V&=\operatorname{CH}^1(S)_\Q\otimes\Q_\ell,\\ C&=\bigl(\operatorname{CH}^2(D_1)_\Q \oplus\operatorname{CH}^2(D_2)_\Q\bigr) \otimes\Q_\ell,\\ G:V&\longrightarrow C, &G(z)&=((i_1)_*z,-(i_2)_*z), \end{aligned} \] where \(i_a:S\hookrightarrow D_a\) are the inclusions. Let \[ \operatorname{cl}_C:C\longrightarrow H^4(\bar D_1,\Q_\ell(2))\oplus H^4(\bar D_2,\Q_\ell(2)) \] be the ordinary cycle map. There is an isomorphism \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{coker}\bigl[ H_M^4(U,\Q(3))\otimes\Q_\ell &\longrightarrow H^4(\bar U,\Q_\ell(3))^\Gamma \bigr]\\ &\simeq\operatorname{im}G\cap\ker\operatorname{cl}_C. \end{split} \] Here \(H_M\) is ordinary rational motivic cohomology and the right-hand cohomology is continuous \(\ell\)-adic cohomology. The identification is canonical after fixing the displayed Mayer--Vietoris orientation and the usual cycle maps.
status: Proved exact comparison formula; no colimit vanishing or survival assertion
notes: The fixed-open cokernel is im of the signed Picard Gysin map intersected with the codimension2 cycle kernel on the two boundary threefolds. No nonzero element is asserted, and fixed-open failure would not imply survival under further shrinking. Method-obstruction calculation, not a smaller universal gate.

statement: Kernel of the ordinary generic Milnor regulator: Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension, and let $\ell\ne p$. Define ordinary generic continuous cohomology by \[ H^n_\eta(K,\mathbf Z_\ell(n)) =\varinjlim_{\varnothing\ne U\subset X} H^n_{\mathrm{cont}}(U,\mathbf Z_\ell(n)), \] where $X$ is a model of $K$ and the limit can be taken over its smooth dense opens. For the ordinary cycle map \[ \rho_n:K_n^M(K)\longrightarrow H^n_\eta(K,\mathbf Z_\ell(n)), \] one has, for every $n\ge0$, \[ \ker\rho_n=\bigcap_{r\ge1}\ell^rK_n^M(K). \tag{B.M1} \] For $n\ge1$, suppose moreover that $X/k$ is smooth projective and that $\alpha\in K_n^M(k(X))$ has infinitely $\ell$-divisible residue at every prime divisor of $X$. Then $\alpha$ is infinitely $\ell$-divisible. The second assertion deliberately excludes $n=0$.
status: Proved intermediate statement; the universal B.1 gate is unchanged
notes: Kernel of the ordinary diagonal-twist Milnor regulator equals intersection of all ell-power multiples, for n>=0. For n>=1 infinitely divisible residues imply infinite divisibility. Degree induction uses negative refined-unramified weights and finite Frobenius orbits; the critical degree3 twist2 has possible weight0, and no arbitrary completed-eigenclass conclusion follows. Not a strictly smaller universal gate.

statement: The separated Milnor quotient is free: In the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:B-Milnor-divisible-kernel}, set \[ D_\ell(K_n)=\bigcap_{r\ge1}\ell^rK_n^M(K),\qquad M_n(K)=K_n^M(K)/D_\ell(K_n). \] Then $D_\ell(K_n)$ is $\ell$-divisible and $M_n(K)$ is a free abelian group of at most countable rank. Moreover, $D_\ell(K_n)$ is independent of the prime $\ell\ne p$. Thus one canonical quotient $M_n(K)$ induces the canonical isomorphisms of completions \[ \widehat{K_n^M(K)}_\ell\simeq\widehat{M_n(K)}_\ell \qquad(\ell\ne p), \] equivariant for the Frobenius action from any finite-field model. No saturated residue embedding or equivariant permutation basis is asserted, and a common integral module does not by itself make its completed Frobenius spectra independent of the prime.
status: Proved intermediate structural consequence; no new universal gate
notes: D_ell is ell-divisible; alteration restriction and residues give the countable free quotient. D_ell maps trivially to every other free quotient M_(ellprime), so all D_ell for ell not equal p coincide. One canonical integral Frobenius quotient gives every prime-to-p completion. No saturated embedding, equivariant permutation basis or prime-independent completed spectrum follows; no priority or qualifying movement claim.

statement: All full rational etale groups, with the defect left visible: For every prime \(\ell\), \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} n&H^0_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))& \dim_{\Q_\ell}H^1_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))& \dim_{\Q_\ell}H^2_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))\\ \hline 0&\Q_\ell&r_2+1+\delta_{K,\ell}(0)&\delta_{K,\ell}(0)\\ 1&0&r_1+r_2-1+|T|&|T|-1\\ n\ge2&0&r_n&0\\ n<0&0&r_n+\delta_{K,\ell}(n)&\delta_{K,\ell}(n). \end{array}\tag{B.10} \] All other degrees vanish. For \(n=1\), more precisely, \[ H^1_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(1))= \mathcal O_{K,T}^\times\otimes\Q_\ell,\qquad H^2_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(1))= \ker\bigl(\Q_\ell^T\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q_\ell\bigr). \tag{B.11} \] For \(n\ge2\), the Chern-class map identifies degree one with \(K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q_\ell\). The defect \(\delta_{K,\ell}(0)\) is exactly the Leopoldt defect. For \(n<0\), writing \(m=1-n\), it is exactly the dimension of the kernel of the \(\ell\)-adic regulator \[ K_{2m-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(m)}\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{v\mid\ell}K_v .\tag{B.12} \] In particular, replacing every defect in (B.10) by zero is equivalent, at the indicated \((K,\ell,n)\), to Leopoldt for \(n=0\), or to Schneider's regulator-injectivity conjecture at \(m=1-n\) for \(n<0\).
status: Proved
notes: Negative-twist defect is strict positive-twist regulator kernel; no unproved vanishing asserted.

statement: An unconditional rational structure in degree one: For every integer \(n\), all primes \(\ell\), and the above geometric local conditions, the natural realization maps give \[ H^1_{f,X}(K,\Q_\ell(n))\simeq V_X(n)\otimes\Q_\ell, \quad V_X(n)= \begin{cases} \mathcal O_{K,S}^\times\otimes\Q,&n=1,\\ K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q,&n\ge2,\\ 0,&n\le0. \end{cases}\tag{B.15} \] In particular the degree-one assertion for negative twists does not require Schneider's conjecture. That conjecture concerns the full groups in (B.10), not the group in (B.15).
status: Proved
notes: S-units for n1, Adams K eigenspaces n>=2, zero n<=0.

statement: The common rational spaces in every Tate degree: For \(X=\Spec\mathcal O_{K,S}\), the following table lists all possibly nonzero common \(\Q\)-spaces \(H^i_{\rm abs}(X,\Q(n))\). The dual in the table is the \(\Q\)-linear dual. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|l} n&i&H^i_{\rm abs}(X,\Q(n))\\ \hline 0&0&\Q\\ 0&2&(\mathcal O_K^\times\otimes\Q)^\vee\\ 1&1&\mathcal O_{K,S}^\times\otimes\Q\\ 1&2&\ker(\Q^S\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q)\\ 1&3&\operatorname{coker}(\Q^S\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q)\\ n\ge2&1&K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q\\ n<0&2&(K_{1-2n}(\mathcal O_K)^{(1-n)}\otimes\Q)^\vee . \end{array} \tag{B.17a} \] Every unlisted group is zero. For every prime \(\ell\), including two, these spaces tensor to the cohomology of the specified Selmer complex with the geometric open-place conditions. Neither Leopoldt nor Schneider is assumed in this assertion.
status: Proved for the specified absolute and Selmer complexes
notes: Complete all-degree/all-twist Q table. Two Poitou-Tate exact sequences give degree2 through chosen splittings, not a claimed canonical derived duality. At removed places twist1 includes full local H2, yielding invariant kernel/cokernel.

statement: A precise conjectural replacement for requirement 4): The following is a comparison \emph{package}, rather than a claim that Bloch--Kato's degree-one conjecture already constructs an absolute category. Its data include enhanced, stable, \(\Q\)-linear categories \(\mathcal A(X)\), with exact unital functors from constructible geometric motives, for finite-type schemes \(X/\Z\). These are the proposed arithmetic completions; their rational cohomology complexes are \[ R\Gamma_{\rm abs}(X,M) =R\Hom_{\mathcal A(X)}(\mathbf1_X,M), \qquad H^i(X,M)=H^iR\Gamma_{\rm abs}(X,M), \] and compatible \(\ell\)-adic arithmetic realization complexes \(\mathsf S_\ell(X,M)\). The complexes have finite-dimensional cohomology, and the regulator is required to be a quasi-isomorphism \[ c_{\ell,X,M}:R\Gamma_{\rm abs}(X,M)\otimes_\Q\Q_\ell \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathsf S_\ell(X,M). \tag{B.18a} \] Here the word ``arithmetic'' is fixed by the following requirements; it does not mean unrestricted cohomology of \(X[1/\ell]\). \begin{enumerate} \item On a smooth projective variety over \(k=\F_q\), the rational complex is the rational motivic Weil--etale complex. For \(\ell\ne p\) its realization is \[ \mathsf S_\ell(X,M)= \operatorname{Cone}\bigl(1-\phi_q: R\Gamma(\bar X,M_\ell)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\bar X,M_\ell)\bigr)[-1]. \] Arithmetic Frobenius and its action are chosen consistently as above. At \(p\), Tate coefficients use the logarithmic Hodge--Witt realization. The conjectural cycle hypothesis is \emph{all three} clauses of Geisser's \(T(Y,r)\), for every smooth projective \(Y\) over finite fields: Tate surjectivity, semisimplicity at one, and rational=numerical equivalence. The normalized arithmetic class is \(e_q\), with restriction \(e_q\mapsto m e_{q^m}\). \item On a proper number ring, prescribe a pure generic motive \(M/K\) together with a geometric extension \(M_X\), or explicit intermediate-extension data, representing the finite condition. The generic motive is not assumed to be lisse on the whole proper ring. The degree-zero and degree-one rational spaces and maps are Fontaine's \(A^a(M)=H_f^a(K,M)\) and \(c^a_\ell\), for \(a=0,1\). For both \(M\) and \(M^*=M^\vee(1)\), these are required to be finite-dimensional and to satisfy f-admissibility. In the geometrically defined case, \(A^1\) is the model-image group of Bloch--Kato, with the homologically trivial cycle group in its middle-degree case. The higher rational spaces are the dual completion \[ A^2(M)=A^1(M^*)^\vee,\qquad A^3(M)=A^0(M^*)^\vee, \] and the realization is the Selmer complex (B.16). Its local degree-one condition is unramified away from \(\ell\), and crystalline \(f\) at retained places above \(\ell\). An arithmetic open uses the geometric \(g\) condition at omitted places above \(\ell\), and the entire local change complex, including its degree-two term. At real places the compact-support complex includes the stated Tate modification; the rational archimedean completion is part of the data. \item For an open--closed decomposition \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\), \(i:Z\hookrightarrow X\), both arithmetic theories have the localization triangles for \(i^!\) and \(j^*\), and the compact-support triangles for \(j_!\) and \(i^*\). The maps (B.18a) commute with these triangles, their boundary maps, proper pushforward, pullback where defined, and finite-extension restriction and trace. For the structural map \(f:X\to\Spec\Z\), the definition is compatible with \[ R\Gamma_{\rm abs}(X,M)= R\Gamma_{\rm abs}(\Spec\Z,Rf_*M), \] and similarly for \(\mathsf S_\ell\) and for compact support. The existence of these compatible extensions to arbitrary constructible geometric coefficients and arbitrary finite-type bases is an \emph{additional conjectural assertion}. It is not deduced merely by naming local subgroups of \(H^1\). \end{enumerate} The first two clauses specify the local and global theories that the extension must preserve. The third states the missing gluing and functoriality assertion expressly. Thus this is an existential conjecture about complexes, maps and compatibilities, rather than an assertion that equal dimensions suffice. The arithmetic degree-zero and degree-one clauses are Bloch--Kato--Fontaine; the finite-field and gluing clauses are the additional requirements needed for the present absolute-cohomology question \cite[Conjecture~5.3]{BBlochKato1990} \cite[\S\S6.5--6.7]{BFontaine1992} \cite[Conjecture~8.3 and Theorem~8.4]{BGeisser2004}.
status: Conjectural formulation; its stated specializations are proved below
notes: Explicit enhanced arithmetic categories, maps, local f/g conditions, chosen model/intermediate-extension data, finite-field Tate-Beilinson clauses, and localization/pushforward gluing. The specializations follow by Geisser and the all-Tate dual completion; general coherent existence remains conjectural.

statement: The two specializations of the corrected package: The finite-field clauses of Definition~\ref{def:B-corrected-comparison-package} imply every \emph{compatible} comparison and cycle-space assertion proved in B.1, including the odd classes and the extension-degree factor. Its number-ring clauses specialize, for every \(M=\Q(n)\), to the unconditional table in Corollary~\ref{cor:B-Hf-all-degrees}. No implication from the arithmetic degree-one clause alone to the finite-field Beilinson clause is used.
status: Proved conditional implications; the Tate number-ring specialization is unconditional
notes: Explicit enhanced arithmetic categories, maps, local f/g conditions, chosen model/intermediate-extension data, finite-field Tate-Beilinson clauses, and localization/pushforward gluing. The specializations follow by Geisser and the all-Tate dual completion; general coherent existence remains conjectural.

statement: Scholbach's ordinary Hom theory is not the full absolute theory: The ordinary motivic cohomology functor used in Scholbach's \emph{f-cohomology and motives over number rings} does not satisfy the full finite-field part of the corrected comparison package. This failure already occurs on an explicitly specified object of its stated category over \(\Spec\Z\).
status: Proved counterexample to the full identification; the source's conditional comparison is retained
notes: For i:SpecFp to SpecZ, N=i_*unit, ordinary Hom degree1 is K_-1(Fp)Q=0 while continuous Qell degree1 is Qell. The actual conditional generic f-comparison is retained; crystalline omission and mixed-motive axioms remain explicit.

statement: The exact support sequence and corank: There is an exact sequence \[ \begin{split} 0\longrightarrow\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow H^1_{\et}(X,A)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{v\mid N\ \mathrm{or}\ v\mid\infty} H^1(K_v,A)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow\mathcal S_\ell(A^t)^D . \end{split}\tag{B.19} \] There is no assertion of surjectivity onto the last term. Put \(d=[K:\Q]\dim A\), \(s=\Bcorank_{\Z_\ell}\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty]\), and let \[ t=\operatorname{rank}_{\Z_\ell}\operatorname{im} \left(\mathcal S_\ell(A^t)\longrightarrow \prod_{v\mid\ell}A^t(K_v)^{\wedge}_\ell\right). \] Then \[ \Bcorank_{\Z_\ell}H^1_{\et}(X,A)[\ell^\infty]=d+s-t. \tag{B.20} \] If \(\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite, then \(t\) is the dimension of the \(\ell\)-adic closure of the Mordell--Weil group \(A^t(K)\) inside its local points. It must not in general be replaced by the abstract rank \(r=\operatorname{rank}A(K)\).
status: Proved
notes: t is local closure rank of pro-Selmer, not abstract Mordell-Weil rank.

statement: Identical global ranks, different arithmetic coranks: Put \(S=\Spec\Z[1/(2\cdot11\cdot37\cdot389)]\), and let \[ \begin{aligned} E_{11}&:y^2+y=x^3-x^2-10x-20,\\ E_{37}&:y^2+y=x^3-x,\\ E_{389}&:y^2+y=x^3+x^2-2x. \end{aligned} \] The abelian schemes \(A=E_{389}\times E_{11}\) and \(B=E_{37}\times E_{37}\) over the same base \(S\) have \[ \begin{gathered} \dim A=\dim B=2,\qquad \operatorname{rank}A(\Q)=\operatorname{rank}B(\Q)=2,\\ \Sha(A/\Q)[2^\infty]=\Sha(B/\Q)[2^\infty]=0. \end{gathered} \] Nevertheless their arithmetic cohomology groups have distinct coranks: \[ \operatorname{corank}_{\Z_2}H^1(S,A)[2^\infty]=1, \qquad \operatorname{corank}_{\Z_2}H^1(S,B)[2^\infty]=0. \] Thus even fixing the number field, coefficient prime, base, dimension, Mordell--Weil rank and entire primary Sha group does not determine the requested arithmetic corank. The local closure contribution \(t\) in Theorem~\ref{thm:B-Sha-corank} is essential.
status: Refuted rank-only determination; explicit corrected coranks proved
notes: Over Z[1/(2*11*37*389)], E389 times E11 and E37 squared both have dimension2, rank2 and zero entire2-primarySha, but local closures rank1 and2. Their H1 primary coranks are1 and0. Every Selmer-basis quartic has rational point(0,1), with exact maps checked. This substantiates an already-refuted rank-only claim and is not new universal-gate movement.

statement: The counterexample in R6, without a BSD assumption: Take \[ E=X_0(11):\quad y^2+y=x^3-x^2-10x-20. \] Its discriminant is \(-11^5\), its conductor is \(11\), and it has good reduction over \(\Z[1/11]\). The reproducible algebraic two-descent in \texttt{part\_b/code/x011.gp} gives \[ \operatorname{ellrank}(E)=[0,0,0,[]],\qquad E(\Q)_{\rm tors}\cong\Z/5, \] with torsion generator \((5,5)\). Thus its rank is certified to be zero; this uses no analytic-rank computation or BSD. PARI's official description of \texttt{ellrank} specifies that the lower and upper bounds and the two-descent data are unconditional. The model of \(X_0(11)\) is also derived explicitly in Elkies's October~13, 2021 lecture notes~\cite{BElkies2021,BPari2026}. For any prime \(\ell\), let \(X=\Spec\Z[1/(11\ell)]\). The Kummer sequence gives \[ 0\longrightarrow E(\Q)\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^1_{\Bcts}(X,V_\ell E) \longrightarrow V_\ell H^1_{\et}(X,E)\longrightarrow0. \] The first term is zero. The global Euler characteristic of \(V_\ell E\), whose complex-conjugation eigenspaces both have dimension one, is \(-1\). Its \(H^0\) is zero, so \(\dim H^1=1+\dim H^2\ge1\). It follows that \(H^1_{\et}(X,E)[\ell^\infty]\) is infinite for every \(\ell\). For \(\ell=2\) the zero two-Selmer calculation additionally gives \(\Sha(E)[2]=0\), hence \(\Sha(E)[2^\infty]=0\); then (B.20) gives exact corank one. All hypotheses of the boxed assertion on 12:75 hold, including invertibility of \(\ell\) on \(X\), and its conclusion fails.
status: Refuted; corrected statement proved
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An arithmetic relative-curve counterexample to 12:79: Let \(S=\Spec\Z[1/22]\) and let \(f:X\to S\) be the smooth proper genus-one curve given by the above model of \(X_0(11)\), with its zero section. Then \[ \left(\Br(X)/f^*\Br(S)\right)[2^\infty] \simeq H^1_{\et}(S,E)[2^\infty] \] has \(\Z_2\)-corank one. Thus surjectivity modulo finite groups of \(\Br(S)\to\Br(X)\) is false for arithmetic bases, even for a smooth proper relative curve with a section.
status: Refuted; corrected statement proved
notes: S=Z[1/22], X=E_S; quotient2-primary corank1. Primary decomposition of torsion quotient is explicitly justified.

statement: Splitting off divisor classes on a smooth open variety: Let \(Y/\F_q\) be smooth, separated and of finite type, and let \(N_Y\) be the image of \(\BPic(\bar Y)\otimes\Q_\ell\) in \(H^2(\bar Y,\Q_\ell(1))\), for \(\ell\ne p\). Then \(N_Y\) is a \(\Gamma\)-equivariant direct summand. No semisimplicity or Tate conjecture for the complementary summand is assumed.
status: Proved
notes: Unconditional; full Frobenius semisimplicity and Tate are not needed.

statement: The finite-field chain over a regular finite-type base: For the smooth separated base \(S\) above, the natural map \[ H^1(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow H^1(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma \] has finite kernel and cokernel. Consequently the following four conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(H^1(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite; \item the Kummer map \(A(S)\otimes\Q_\ell\to H^1_{\Bcts}(S,V_\ell A)\) is an isomorphism; \item the same map to \(W^\Gamma\) is an isomorphism; \item \(H^1(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma\) is finite. \end{enumerate} These are equivalences, without an assumption that their equivalent finiteness assertions hold. If \(S\) is projective and \(A\) is constant, these assertions of finiteness hold unconditionally.
status: Proved
notes: Algebraic divisor subspace splits on smooth open via Hodge index, weights, alteration trace. [a] eigenspace on total dual abelian scheme splits geometric Kummer; cofiniteness promotes rational isomorphism to finite kernel and cokernel.

statement: Relative curves without a section: Let \(S/\F_q\) be smooth, separated and connected of finite type, and let \(f:Y\to S\) be a smooth proper curve with geometrically connected fibres and relative Jacobian \(J\). For \(\ell\ne p\), \[ V_\ell\bigl(\Br(Y)/\operatorname{im}\Br(S)\bigr) \simeq V_\ell H^1(S,J). \tag{B.32} \] The kernel of \(\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\to\Br(Y)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite. Consequently the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(\Br(S)\to\Br(Y)\) is surjective modulo a finite \(\ell\)-primary group; \item \(H^1(S,J)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite; \item \(H^1(\bar S,\bar J)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma\) is finite. \end{enumerate} If \(f\) has a section, the natural edge map gives the stronger integral isomorphism \[ (\Br(Y)/\Br(S))[\ell^\infty] \simeq H^1(S,J)[\ell^\infty]. \]
status: Proved
notes: A Cartier closure supplies degree d, not a finite multisection. Rational Leray and Picard identify the quotient Tate module; cofinite torsion gives equivalence modulo finite groups.

statement: A source error avoided in the preceding proof: Keller's Lemma~2.17 claims that the closure of a generic-fibre point of a proper relative curve is finite over an integral base. This is false in the printed generality. Over any finite field take \(S=\mathbb A^2_{x,y}\), \(Y=\mathbb P^1_{[u:v]}\times S\), and the generic point \([u:v]=[x:y]\). Its closure is \(uy-vx=0\), the blowup of the origin, whose fibre over \((0,0)\) is the whole \(\mathbb P^1\). On its two standard charts the coordinate rings are \(k[x,t]\), \(y=xt\), and \(k[y,s]\), \(x=ys\); it is integral and has no additional irreducible component. This explicitly contradicts the lemma's quasi-finiteness step. The degree of the associated line bundle, which is all the proof above uses, remains one on every fibre. Thus the section-free part of the preceding proposition is not inherited from that lemma or from its use in Corollary~2.18 and Theorem~4.27~\cite[Lemma~2.17]{BKeller2016}.
status: Refuted; corrected statement proved
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Sections and their completion on a reduced base: Let \(S/\F_q\) be reduced and of finite type, without a separatedness assumption, and let \(A/S\) be an abelian scheme. Put \(C_S=A(\bar S)\). Then \(C_S/(C_S)_{\rm tors}\) is finitely generated, its Galois action has finite image, and the natural map gives an isomorphism \[ C_S\otimes_{\Z}\Q_\ell \xrightarrow{\sim} (C_S)^{\wedge}_\ell\otimes_{\Z_\ell}\Q_\ell \qquad (\ell\ne p). \] There exists a finite disjoint union \(V\) of smooth separated finite-type \(\F_q\)-schemes with a jointly surjective map \(v:V\to S\). Pullback embeds \(C_S\) in \(C_V\) and embeds their quotients by torsion.
status: Proved
notes: Reduced-base section injection and LangNeron give finite free quotient; ell torsion embeds in finitely many Pruefer groups, so completion rationalization agrees with tensor Qell.

statement: The finite-field chain for arbitrary finite-type schemes: Let \(S/\F_q\) be any scheme of finite type, let \(A/S\) be an abelian scheme, and let \(\ell\ne p\), including \(\ell=2\) when \(p\ne2\). No regularity, reducedness, properness or separatedness of \(S\) is required. Set \[ W_S=H^1_{\Bcts}(\bar S,V_\ell A),\qquad N_S=A(\bar S)\otimes\Q_\ell. \] The geometric Kummer sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow N_S\longrightarrow W_S \longrightarrow V_\ell H^1_{\et}(\bar S,\bar A) \longrightarrow0 \] has a \(\Gamma\)-equivariant splitting. The natural map \[ H^1_{\et}(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow H^1_{\et}(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma \] has finite kernel and cokernel. The four conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-finite-chain-proper} are therefore equivalent for every such \(S\).
status: Proved
notes: Section space embeds in the finite-Galois section representation of a jointly surjective smooth alteration cover. Averaging a linear projection and composing its Kummer retraction proves the splitting without hypercover descent.

statement: Why the positive-degree argument retains its regularity hypothesis: There is a reduced projective surface \(S/\F_2\) and a smooth proper genus-one scheme \(f:X\to S\) for which every global line bundle has relative degree zero. Thus the positive-degree class used in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-relative-curve} cannot be asserted on an arbitrary singular base. This example does not assert that the Brauer quotient is infinite. Take \[ E:\ y^2z+yz^2+x^3+x^2z=0\ \subset T=\mathbf P^2_{\F_2}, \qquad O=[0:1:0], \qquad S=T\amalg_E T. \] The derivatives of the cubic are \(x^2,z^2,y^2+x^2\), with no common projective zero, so \(E\) is an elliptic curve. The pushout is the explicit finite \(T\)-scheme \[ S=\operatorname{Spec}_T(\mathcal O_T\oplus\mathcal O_T(-3)), \qquad R[t]/(t(t-f_E))\simeq R\times_{R/(f_E)}R \] on each trivializing affine, where multiplication on the second summand uses the cubic section \(f_E\). It is reduced because the displayed algebra embeds in the product of two domains, and projective because it is finite over \(T\). Let \(A=E\times S\). The closed-cover sequence on the small etale site is \[ 0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_{1*}A_T\oplus i_{2*}A_T \xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_1-\mathrm{res}_2}i_{E*}A_E \longrightarrow0. \] For surjectivity it suffices to pass to a strict henselian local ring. A section into the smooth curve \(E\) on its closed quotient lifts across the resulting henselian pair; see the Stacks Project, Lemma~15.13.3~\cite{BStacksSmoothLift}. The kernel is the fibre-product description of \(S\). Every map \(\mathbf P^2\to E\) is constant, since its restriction to each projective line is constant, whereas the rigidity lemma gives \[ A(T)=E(\F_2),\qquad A(E)=E(\F_2)\oplus\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E). \] The cohomology boundary therefore injects \(\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E)\) into \(H^1_{\et}(S,A)\). In particular \(\alpha=\delta(1_E)\) has infinite order: \([m]:E\to E\) has degree \(m^2\) and is nonconstant for every nonzero integer \(m\). To represent this class by a scheme, glue two copies \(X_i=E\times T\) along \(E\times E\), using the identity on one side and \((a,t)\mapsto(a+t,t)\) on the other. Both attaching maps are closed immersions, so the pushout is a scheme by the Stacks Project, Lemma~37.67.8; Lemma~37.67.9(4) gives smoothness over \(S\)~\cite{BStacksClosedPushout,BStacksPushoutMorphisms}. The same local lifting just used trivializes the translation cocycle on an etale cover. Thus this scheme is the \(A\)-torsor of class \(\pm\alpha\), locally isomorphic to \(E\times S\), and is proper with geometrically connected genus-one fibres. Under the principal polarization \(E\simeq E^\vee\), translation by \(a\) acts on \(\operatorname{Pic}^d(E)\) by translation by \(\pm da\): represent a divisor by its sum in \(E\). Consequently \(\operatorname{Pic}^d_{X/S}\) is a torsor of class \(\pm d\alpha\). A global line bundle of degree \(d\) would give a section of that torsor, forcing \(d\alpha=0\), hence \(d=0\). This proves the assertion, and also shows that \(X\to S\) is not projective. The cubic smoothness, its five \(\F_2\)-points, and the displayed fibre-product algebra were checked exactly by \texttt{part\_b/code/singular\_genus\_one\_checks.py}; its output is preserved with the computations. The infinite-order and torsor claims are proved above, not inferred from the finite computation.
status: Proved counterexample to an extension beyond the stated manuscript scope
notes: S is two P2 overF2 glued along the explicit smooth elliptic cubic. Translation by id_E glues a proper smooth genus-one torsor of infinite period. Pic^d has class d alpha, so every line bundle has degree0. This is not a Brauer-infinitude counterexample and lies outside the regular scope of12:79.

statement: A fully specified nonzero degree-two group on 12:78: Let \(C/\F_2\) be the good reduction of the displayed \(X_0(11)\) model, and let \(A=C\times C\to C\) be its constant Jacobian scheme. Take \(\ell=3\). Direct enumeration gives \(\#C(\F_2)=5\), so Frobenius on \(V_3C\) has polynomial \(t^2+2t+2\). Its two roots are distinct, and the centralizer of a companion matrix has dimension two. Kummer, the constant-case result just proved, and Hochschild--Serre give \[ V_3H^2_{\et}(C,A) \simeq H^2_{\Bcts}(C,V_3A) \simeq H^1_{\Bcts}(\bar C,V_3A)_\Gamma \simeq\End_{\F_2}(C)\otimes\Q_3, \] of dimension two. The geometric degree-two term has weight one, so contributes no invariants; in the degree-one term, \(H^1(\bar C,\Q_3)\otimes V_3C=(V_3C)^\vee\otimes V_3C\). Semisimplicity identifies its coinvariants with its invariants, and Tate's Main Theorem identifies the latter with endomorphisms. The point count and exact centralizer calculation are reproduced in \texttt{part\_b/code/finite\_field\_checks.py}. This verifies the intended nonvanishing in R6. If a dual Tate module is replaced in the transcription by the Tate module of the dual abelian variety, a twist must be retained: \((V_\ell J)^\vee=V_\ell(J^t)(-1)\). An integral isomorphism also cannot be read off from a displayed \(\Q_\ell\)-vector-space calculation without tracking finite Kummer kernels.
status: Proved
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The prime-to-characteristic relative-curve gate is a surface gate: Fix primes \(p\ne\ell\). The following statements are equivalent. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The Tate conjecture for divisors holds for every smooth projective surface over \(\F_p\), including connected surfaces whose field of constants is a finite extension of \(\F_p\). \item For every finite field \(k/\F_p\), every smooth separated finite-type \(k\)-scheme \(S\), and every smooth projective morphism \(f:X\to S\) with geometrically connected curve fibres, the cokernel of \[ f^*:\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow\Br(X)[\ell^\infty] \] is finite. Here \(\Br=H^2_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\Gm)_{\mathrm{tors}}\) is the cohomological Brauer group. \item The assertion in (ii) holds just for smooth curve families with a section over nonempty opens of \(\mathbb P^1_k\), for all finite \(k/\F_p\). \item The single birational invariant vanishes: \[ H^3(F_0\mathbb P^3_{\overline{\F}_p},\Q_\ell(2))^ {\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\F}_p/\F_p)}=0. \] Here \(F_0\) denotes the colimit over dense open subsets, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate}. \end{enumerate} Thus the universal regular separated-base relative-curve question in its intended \(\ell\ne p\) form is already equivalent to a fixed-dimensional surface conjecture. This theorem does not identify the characteristic-primary assertion with that conjecture, and does not extend its surface equivalence to arbitrary singular or nonseparated bases.
status: Proved equivalence; the equivalent surface Tate assertion remains unresolved
notes: Smooth separated bases and smooth projective geometrically connected curve families, all finite constant extensions. Equivalent already to families with a section over opens ofP1. Reverse direction retains nonproper arithmetic H1(Gamma,H1) and kills only the relative pure-weight-minus1 quotient. No assertion for singular/nonseparated bases or characteristic-primary torsion.

statement: Rational sections descend through proper covers: Let \(S\) be a noetherian \(\F_p\)-scheme, let \(q:T\to S\) be proper and surjective, and let \(A/S\) be an abelian scheme. The sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow A(S)\otimes\Q \longrightarrow A(T)\otimes\Q \xrightarrow{\operatorname{pr}_1^*-\operatorname{pr}_2^*} A(T\times_S T)\otimes\Q \] is exact. The same equalizer statement holds after scalar extension from \(\Q\) to \(\Q_\ell\).
status: Proved
notes: The graph image is a finite universal homeomorphism; uniform Frobenius factorization followed by Verschiebung descends a p-power multiple. Rational equalizers extend to Qell by flatness, without clearing arbitrary Qell coefficients.

statement: The universal all-base finiteness gate: Fix distinct primes \(p\) and \(\ell\). The following universal assertions are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item Divisor Tate holds for every smooth projective surface over every finite extension of \(\F_p\). \item For every finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\) and every abelian scheme \(A/S\), the group \(H^1_{\et}(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite. No regularity, reducedness, properness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed on \(S\). \item The assertion in (2) holds for the Jacobians of smooth projective geometrically connected curve families with a section over nonempty opens of \(\mathbf P^1\), over all finite extensions of \(\F_p\). \end{enumerate} These assertions are also equivalent to the birational degree-three vanishing in Theorem~\ref{thm:B-relative-surface-gate}.
status: Proved equivalence; the surface Tate assertion is unresolved
notes: Smooth total dual abelian scheme and multiplication eigenspace give invariant Kummer surjectivity. Proper Cech descent has weight-minus1 H1 pullback kernel, and rational sections descend. Nilpotent and finite-open descent include nonreduced/nonseparated bases. The separate integral torsor-lattice and all-base unit-cup theorems now resolve the singular relative-Picard and Brauer base-image passages under the same surface-Tate hypothesis.

statement: Finite generation of the localized torsor group: Assume the equivalent surface-Tate conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-all-bases-surface-gate}. For every finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\), every abelian scheme \(A/S\), and every \(\ell\ne p\), \[ H^1_{\et}(S,A)\otimes\Z_{(\ell)} \quad\hbox{is finitely generated over }\Z_{(\ell)}. \tag{B.24i} \] Thus the non-torsion part on a singular base is controlled as well as its \(\ell\)-primary torsion. If \(f:X\to S\) is a smooth proper family of geometrically connected curves, then \[ H^1_{\et}(S,\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S})[\ell^\infty] \quad\hbox{is finite}, \] even when its degree-one Picard torsor has infinite order.
status: Proved conditional strengthening; surface Tate remains unresolved
notes: For every finite-type base, H1(S,A) tensor Z_(ell) is finitely generated. The proper-cover kernel injects after inverting p into a finite-rank Cech group; torsor graph descent uses Frobenius and Verschiebung. Consequently the relative Picard H1 has finite ell torsion even for infinite-period singular-base degree classes.

statement: The integral degree-two kernel of a cover: Let \(q:T\to S\) be a morphism of finite-type \(\F_p\)-schemes whose perfection is a \(v\)-cover, and put \(T_a=T\times_S\cdots\times_ST\) with \(a+1\) factors. Then \[ \ker\bigl(H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)[1/p] \longrightarrow H^2_{\et}(T,\Gm)[1/p]\bigr) \] is a finitely generated \(\Z[1/p]\)-module. Consequently, for every prime \(\ell\ne p\), the same kernel after tensoring with \(\Z_{(\ell)}\) is finitely generated over \(\Z_{(\ell)}\). These are assertions about the full cohomology groups, including their possible non-torsion parts. In particular the lemma applies to proper surjections and to finite-type \(h\)-covers obtained by combining a finite open cover with proper surjections.
status: Proved without a Tate hypothesis
notes: Degree-two etale-to-v injection uses only epsilon_*Gm=Gm and R1epsilon_*Gm=0. Kernel filtration is bounded by Pic(T1)[1/p] and units(T2)[1/p]. Applies to finite-type h-covers combining affine opens and proper alterations, including nonseparated bases. No all-degree derived Gm comparison claimed.

statement: Proper singular bases introduce no further prime-to-\(p\) gate: Fix \(p\ne\ell\). Divisor Tate for all smooth projective surfaces over finite extensions of \(\F_p\) is equivalent to the following assertion: \[ \begin{gathered} H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)\otimes\Z_{(\ell)} \quad\hbox{is a finitely generated }\Z_{(\ell)}\hbox{-module}\\ \hbox{for every proper finite-type }\F_p\hbox{-scheme }S. \end{gathered} \tag{B.24h} \] Under these equivalent hypotheses, \(\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite for every such \(S\), including singular and nonreduced ones. In particular, if \(S\) is proper and \(f:X\to S\) is a proper curve family, the \(\ell\)-primary cokernel of \(\Br(S)\to\Br(X)\) is finite, whether or not there is a global positive-degree line bundle on that family.
status: Proved equivalence; the surface Tate assertion remains unresolved
notes: Properness kills the arithmetic weight-minus1 term. Full H2 may retain a free lattice; only its ell-primary torsion is asserted finite. Includes singular and nonreduced proper schemes.

statement: Arithmetic unit cups generate the smooth Brauer group up to finite error: Fix a finite field \(k\) of characteristic \(p\) and a prime \(\ell\ne p\). Assume divisor Tate for all smooth projective surfaces over finite extensions of \(k\). For every smooth quasi-projective finite-type \(k\)-scheme \(T\), the cyclic-cup map \[ c_T:\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T^\times)\otimes \Q_\ell/\Z_\ell \longrightarrow \Br(T)[\ell^\infty] \tag{B.24j'} \] has finite cokernel. Here \(u\otimes a/\ell^r\) maps to the cyclic class \((\chi_{a/r},u)\), where the arithmetic character \(\chi_{a/r}:\Gal(\bar k/k)\to \Q_\ell/\Z_\ell\) sends arithmetic Frobenius to \(a/\ell^r\). The construction is natural for every \(k\)-morphism.
status: Proved conditional on divisor Tate for surfaces
notes: Unit Kummer classes comprise the weight-zero H1(1) part; quotient pure weight-minus1. Alteration trace is norm on units, with ample hypotheses satisfied by quasi-projectivity. HochschildSerre arithmetic cup gives rational Tate-module surjectivity, hence finite cokernel.

statement: Unit cups have finite kernel on every finite-type base: Let \(k\) be a finite field of characteristic \(p\), let \(\ell\ne p\), and let \(U\) be any finite-type \(k\)-scheme. The natural cyclic-cup map \[ c_U:\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times)\otimes \Q_\ell/\Z_\ell \longrightarrow\Br(U)[\ell^\infty] \] from Lemma~\ref{lem:B-unit-cup-generation} has finite kernel. No separatedness, reducedness, or smoothness hypothesis on \(U\) is required.
status: Proved without a Tate hypothesis
notes: Finitely many divisorial valuations of generic fields inject the unit lattice. Residues multiply by valuation and finite constant-field degree; a full-rank integer matrix has finite kernel on the associated Pruefer groups. Singular, nonreduced, and nonseparated bases included.

statement: The full arbitrary-base Brauer assertion has the surface-Tate gate: Fix \(p\ne\ell\), put \(R=\Z_{(\ell)}\) and \(D=\Q_\ell/\Z_\ell\), and for a finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\) put \[ A_S=H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)\otimes R, \qquad C_S=\operatorname{im} \bigl(c_S:\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S^\times)\otimes D \longrightarrow A_S\bigr). \] The following universal assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Divisor Tate holds for every smooth projective surface over every finite extension of \(\F_p\). \item \(A_S/C_S\) is a finitely generated \(R\)-module for every finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\). \item Unit cups generate \(\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\) up to a finite cokernel for every such \(S\). \end{enumerate} In particular, under these equivalent hypotheses, \[ \bigl(H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)/H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)_{\rm tors}\bigr) \otimes R \] is finitely generated for every \(S\). These statements include nonproper, singular, nonreduced, and nonseparated bases.
status: Proved equivalence; divisor Tate for surfaces remains unresolved
notes: A/C is finitely generated: the restriction kernel is a quotient of a finite-rank lattice and the image is uniformly bounded torsion inside a finite-cotype group. Therefore Br(S)[ell infinity]/C finite for every finite-type base. This closes the singular nonproper base-image gate, without proving surface Tate.

statement: Relative Brauer finiteness over every finite-type base: Assume the equivalent assertions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-all-bases-Brauer-units}. If \(f:X\to S\) is a morphism of finite-type \(\F_p\)-schemes such that pullback identifies their global unit groups, then \[ \operatorname{coker}\bigl( \Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow \Br(X)[\ell^\infty]\bigr) \] is finite. In particular this holds for every smooth proper morphism with geometrically connected fibres, including every curve family in B.3 over an arbitrary finite-type base. Conversely, the universal assertion for those curve families implies divisor Tate for all smooth projective surfaces over finite extensions of \(\F_p\).
status: Proved equivalence with the universal surface-Tate assertion
notes: Proper smooth geometrically connected families preserve global units even over nonreduced bases, hence the total unit-cup subgroup comes from the base. Its finite quotient proves actual Brauer cokernel finiteness. Includes singular/nonproper/nonseparated bases; characteristic-primary counterexample remains distinct.

statement: Prime-uniform generation by arithmetic unit cups: Let \(k\) be a finite field of characteristic \(p\), and assume divisor Tate for all smooth projective surfaces over finite extensions of \(k\), at one fixed prime \(\ell_0\ne p\). Put \(D=(\Q/\Z)[p']\). For every smooth quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(T\), arithmetic cyclic cups give a map \[ c_T:\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T^\times)\otimes D \longrightarrow \Br(T)[p'] \] with finite cokernel. The cokernel is one finite group across all primes different from \(p\); separate finiteness of its primary components is not substituted for this assertion.
status: Proved conditional on divisor Tate for surfaces
notes: H2(Gamma,geometric units) is generated onto by arithmetic unit cups; H1(Gamma,Pic) is one finite group. Geometric prime-uniform finiteness and integral alteration trace give bounded quotient by a divisible subgroup; its fixed-exponent torsion is finite by Kummer. No all-primes finite-cotype claim is used.

statement: Whole prime-to-characteristic Brauer finiteness and the exact gate: Fix \(p\), put \(R=\Z[1/p]\) and \(D=(\Q/\Z)[p']\), and for every finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\) define \[ A_S=H^2_{\et}(S,\Gm)\otimes R, \qquad C_S=\operatorname{im} \bigl(\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S^\times)\otimes D\to A_S\bigr). \] The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Divisor Tate holds, at one prime different from \(p\), for all smooth projective surfaces over all finite extensions of \(\F_p\). \item \(A_S/C_S\) is a finitely generated \(R\)-module for every finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme \(S\). \item \(\Br(S)[p']/C_S\) is a finite group for every such \(S\). \item The whole prime-to-\(p\) Brauer cokernel is finite for every proper smooth geometrically connected curve family over every such \(S\). \end{enumerate} Under these conditions the relative Brauer conclusion also holds for every finite-type morphism identifying global units, in particular every smooth proper morphism with geometrically connected fibres, in arbitrary relative dimension. All statements include singular, nonreduced, nonproper, and nonseparated bases.
status: Proved equivalence; the surface-Tate condition remains unresolved
notes: Full H2(Gm)[1/p] modulo arithmetic unit cups is finitely generated over Z[1/p]. Hence Br(S)[p-prime]/cups is one finite group, and every units-preserving morphism has finite whole prime-to-p Brauer cokernel. Includes all singular, nonreduced, nonproper and nonseparated bases and all smooth proper geometrically connected relative dimensions.

statement: Prime-uniform abelian torsors and an integral lattice: Under the equivalent conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-Brauer-prime-uniform}, every abelian scheme \(A/S\) over a finite-type \(\F_p\)-scheme satisfies \[ H^1_{\et}(S,A)[p']\ \text{finite}, \qquad H^1_{\et}(S,A)\otimes\Z[1/p] \ \text{finitely generated over }\Z[1/p]. \] Conversely, the universal first assertion implies the surface-Tate condition. These are statements about one whole prime-to-\(p\) group, including all primes simultaneously. They include nonreduced and nonseparated bases and abelian schemes without a chosen global polarization.
status: Proved equivalence with the same unresolved surface-Tate condition
notes: For B=A-dual, H1(S,PicB/S) injects in H2(B,Gm) disjoint from the base. The kernel from H1(S,A) is killed by2 and has finite prime-to-p part. Uniform relative Brauer finiteness gives H1(S,A)[p-prime] finite on every finite-type base; existing proper/open Cech descent gives H1(S,A)[1/p] finitely generated. No polarization or constant NS assumption.

statement: The prime in the divisor conjecture for a surface: Let \(Y\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral surface over a finite field \(k\) of characteristic \(p\). Surjectivity of \[ \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\otimes\Q_\ell\longrightarrow H^2(Y_{\bar k},\Q_\ell(1))^{\Gamma_k} \] for one \(\ell\ne p\) is equivalent to its surjectivity for every \(\ell\ne p\). It is also equivalent to the multiplicity of the eigenvalue \(1\) of Frobenius on \(H^2(Y_{\bar k},\Q_\ell(1))\) being \(\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{NS}(Y_{\bar k})^{\Gamma_k}\).
status: Proved
notes: Tate at one prime makes the invariant subspace nondegenerate. Its orthogonal complement has invertible Frob-minus1, so generalized eigenvalue1 multiplicity equals invariant NS rank and is prime independent. No general Frobenius semisimplicity conjecture.

statement: A smaller surface test class: vanishing coherent irregularity: Fix a finite field \(k\) and a prime \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\). The divisor Tate conjecture at \(\ell\) for every smooth projective geometrically integral surface over \(k\) is equivalent to the same assertion restricted to surfaces \(Y/k\) satisfying \[ H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0. \] Consequently every assertion of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-relative-surface-gate}, and the equivalent universal relative Brauer assertions proved above, can be tested using only these surfaces over the finite extensions of \(\F_p\). This is a proper subclass restriction: for an elliptic curve \(E/k\), the surface \(E\times\mathbb P^1_k\) has \(\dim_kH^1(\mathcal O)=1\) and is excluded. The restricted hypothesis imposes only the displayed intrinsic vanishing; it does not retain an arbitrary original surface as auxiliary data.
status: Proved equivalence; the restricted Tate conjecture remains unresolved
notes: Published fixed-field reduction uses a semistable pencil, constant/ample Hodge decomposition over k(t), a regular projective model, and high-degree finite-field Bertini sections. Zero-dimensional ample factor is treated separately. Consequently whole prime-to-p torsor and relative Brauer universal finiteness have this smaller surface test class.

statement: Sources and scope of the reduction: \citet[Remark~4.13, p.~56]{BErtlKellerQin2025} points to the all-dimensional reduction and the additional restriction above. The existing Kahn--Morrow reduction supplies the passage from arbitrary dimension to surfaces; Yuan's Theorem~1.6 supplies the further vanishing of coherent irregularity. Yuan's cited Nguyen thesis and K\"unnemann--Faltings--Chai inputs are used through his exact published statements and proof; they are not represented as independently opened here. De Jong's unpublished reduction note has not been obtained. None of these reductions proves the Tate conjecture for the remaining irregularity-zero surfaces.
status: Verified source scope
notes: Root and D opened published Yuan pp1964-2000; B opened author version Theorem1.6, fullSections4.1-4.2pp32-35. Nguyen thesis and original degeneration inputs are used through Yuan and not represented as separately opened; deJong unpublished reduction note not obtained.

statement: Canonical surfaces suffice, with arbitrary numerical thresholds: Fix a finite field \(k\), a prime \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\), an integer \(N\ge1\), and a real number \(\varepsilon>0\). Divisor Tate at \(\ell\) for every smooth projective geometrically integral surface over \(k\) is equivalent to its restriction to surfaces \(Y/k\) with \[ H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0,\qquad \omega_Y\text{ very ample}, \qquad K_Y^2\ge N,\qquad p_g(Y)\ge N, \] and, if desired, the simultaneous extra conditions \[ c_2(Y)>0,\qquad \left|\frac{K_Y^2}{c_2(Y)}-1\right|<\varepsilon. \] Here \(c_2(Y)=\deg c_2(T_Y)\). Thus the preceding universal Brauer and abelian-torsor gates can be confined to an intrinsic class of canonically embedded surfaces of general type. This does not assert Tate for those surfaces.
status: Proved strict test-class reduction; the restricted Tate conjecture remains unresolved
notes: Pad the two-dimensional model by P1, then retain a smooth threefold until the final arbitrarily high-degree cut. The same cut forces very ample canonical bundle, any prescribed lower bounds for K2 and pg, and positive c2 with K2/c2 arbitrarily close to1. All are bundled as one intrinsic restriction, not separate later gate movements. Universal restricted Tate remains unresolved.

statement: A geometrically simply connected surface test: Fix a finite field \(k\) of characteristic \(p\), a prime \(\ell\ne p\), an integer \(N\geq1\), and a real number \(\varepsilon>0\). Divisor Tate for all smooth projective geometrically integral surfaces over \(k\) is equivalent to divisor Tate for just those surfaces \(Y/k\) satisfying \[ \pi_1^{\et}(Y_{\overline k})=1, \qquad H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0, \qquad \omega_Y\text{ very ample}, \] and, simultaneously, \[ K_Y^2\geq N,\qquad p_g(Y)\geq N,\qquad c_2(Y)>0, \qquad \left|\frac{K_Y^2}{c_2(Y)}-1\right|<\varepsilon. \] No extension of the fixed field \(k\) is needed in the reduction. Consequently the universal prime-to-characteristic torsor and relative-Brauer finiteness assertions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-Brauer-prime-uniform} and Corollary~\ref{cor:B-torsors-prime-uniform} have this smaller intrinsic surface test class, when quantified over finite constant extensions as before. The numerical conditions are inherited from Corollary~\ref{cor:B-canonical-surface-gate}, not independent additional reductions.
status: Proved strict intrinsic test-class equivalence; restricted Tate unresolved
