status: Proved; finite existence is unconditional, and effectiveness has the stated input condition
notes: Removes C+ even over an arbitrary Weil coefficient field. Actual general Chow vanishings and the demanded K3 vanishing remain unresolved.

statement: A finite power detects all the relations: In Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion}, let $r_\nu$ be the input arity of $P_\nu$ and put \[ B=\max\{2,\ 2n+1,\ 2a(b+1),\ r_1,\ldots,r_s\}. \] Then all rational cohomological relations hold in Chow on every power of $X$ if and only if the cycle map is injective on $T_B^{\CH}(X,o)$. In particular such a finite cut-off exists without $C^+(X)$ or a rational form of the Weil cohomology. Its effective construction has exactly the coefficient-data qualification in the theorem.
status: Proved; the cut-off is effective with the same coefficient input
notes: B=max(2,2n+1,2a(b+1),arities of the finite form relations). Does not provide an algorithm for rational equivalence.

statement: A coefficient-independent recursive elimination bound: For integers $v,d\geq1$, let $\mathcal B(v,d)$ be the tree of finite sequences $(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{r-1})$ in $\Z_{\geq0}^v$ satisfying \[ |\alpha_i|\leq d2^i, \qquad \alpha_j\not\leq\alpha_i\quad(0\leq j<i<r), \] where $\leq$ is coordinatewise. This is a finite tree. Its maximum sequence length $\mathcal L(v,d)$ is a total computable integer-valued function. Put \[ \mathcal D(v,d)=d\,2^{\mathcal L(v+1,d)}. \] Over any field, an ideal in $v$ ordinary polynomial variables generated in degrees at most $d$ has, for every monomial order, a Gr\"obner basis in degrees at most $\mathcal D(v,d)$. In particular this bound applies to an elimination order.
status: Proved
notes: No disputed closed Dube formula is imported. The bound is a total recursive function with no efficiency claim.

statement: A uniform arity bound for rational cohomology tables: Suppose the graded Weil cohomology algebra in Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} has a rational table. This includes rational Betti cohomology over $\C$. Put $q=2n$, $u=a-1$, $v=b$, $s=u+v$, and \[ M_0=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{q}\bigl(s^m+(u-v)^m\bigr),\qquad M_1=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{q}\bigl(s^m-(u-v)^m\bigr). \] Define the following integers using the function of the preceding lemma: \[ O=M_1+4uv,\qquad E=M_0+2(u^2+v^2)+2,\qquad J=2^O,\qquad P=E+J, \] \[ D=\mathcal D(P,q+2),\qquad B_{n,a,b}=\max\{2,\ q+1,\ 2a(b+1),\ q(D-1+M_1)\}. \] Then all the point-and-diagonal cohomological relations hold in rational Chow on all powers if and only if the cycle map is injective on $T_{B_{n,a,b}}^{\CH}(X,o)$. The bound depends only on $(n,a,b)$, and is a total computable integer. It is not a practical or minimal bound, and does not decide the required Chow injectivity.
status: Proved in the stated rational-table scope
notes: All super orbit equations have degree at most 2n+1 with rational coefficients. The enormous recursive bound is not evaluated and does not settle any actual K3 Chow vanishing.

statement: The coefficient qualification in the uniform bound: The finite criterion and finite cut-off of Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} and Corollary~\ref{c:finite-power-cutoff} apply to an arbitrary Weil field. The displayed bound depending only on $(n,a,b)$ has the additional rational-table hypothesis. For a presented coefficient algebra whose $h$ named generators include every coordinate of $t=(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_q)$, with its exact defining ideal generated in degrees at most $e$, the same proof gives a bound by adding $h$ to $E$ and replacing the generator-degree input $q+2$ by $\max(q+3,e+1)$. The extra one accounts for a structure constant occurring as a variable in an orbit equation. These $h$ coefficient variables are eliminated together with the group variables, so the result is the rational contraction $I_\Q$. We make no uniform rational-contraction claim for unspecified elements of an arbitrary coefficient field. The accompanying exact certificate exhausts only $\mathcal L(1,d)=d+1$ for $1\leq d\leq4$ and $\mathcal L(2,1)=4$, and checks the square-zero elimination mechanism for the explicit super map $z=x$, $\theta_1=\eta$, $\theta_2=x\eta$. It does not evaluate the enormous geometric cut-off above. No closed Dub\'e degree formula is used in its proof.
status: Proved scope clarification
notes: For a presented coefficient algebra, all form coordinates are named generators and their variables are eliminated. Finite checks cover five small trees and one super orbit graph only.

statement: What the finite criterion settles: Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} removes the sign hypothesis from the finite criterion, including for an arbitrary Weil coefficient field. It supplies finite generators for the all-power obstruction and does not assert that these cycles vanish for every variety. It also does not make rational equivalence decidable. Its list is not claimed minimal; in particular the more precise K3 obstruction identified above is unchanged. The explicitly requested all-power K3 assertion and the unrestricted evaluation of the criterion for every $(X,o)$ therefore remain separate unresolved parts of C.1(c). If $n=0$, connectedness over the algebraically closed field gives $X=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, and every relation holds immediately.
status: Proved scope statement; the actual general Chow vanishing remains unresolved
notes: Finite existence and effective construction are distinguished from deciding the Chow identities. The zero-dimensional point is immediate.

statement: The narrow K3 ring already detects finite-dimensionality: Let $S/\C$ be a projective K3 surface and let $o$ be its Beauville--Voisin class. The following assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item for every $k$, all the cohomological relations among the point and diagonal classes hold in $\CH^*(S^k)_\Q$; \item with $\pi_2=\Delta_S-o\times S-S\times o$, the cycle \begin{equation} D_{23}=\sum_{\sigma\in S_{23}}\sgn(\sigma) \prod_{a=1}^{23}(\pi_2)_{a,23+\sigma(a)} \quad\text{vanishes in }\CH^{46}(S^{46})_\Q; \end{equation} \item $\bigwedge^{23}h^2(S)=0$ in rational Chow motives; \item $h(S)$ is finite-dimensional in the sense of Kimura--O'Sullivan. \end{enumerate} Thus the request for every K3 surface is not supplied by the Beauville--Voisin small-diagonal theorem. The first missing universal determinant for this narrower ring occurs on $46$ factors.
status: Proved equivalence; the general vanishing is unresolved
notes: First missing narrow determinant is on46 factors; equivalent transcendental test is on2(23-rho) factors, using divisor projectors; general vanishing not proved.

statement: Removing the algebraic part of the K3 gate: Let $S/\C$ be a projective K3 surface of Picard rank $\rho$, let $D_1,\ldots,D_\rho$ be a rational basis of $\operatorname{NS}(S)_\Q$, and let $B=(\deg D_aD_b)_{a,b}$. Define \[ \pi_{\rm alg}=\sum_{a,b}(B^{-1})_{ab}D_a\times D_b, \qquad \pi_{\rm tr}=\pi_2-\pi_{\rm alg},\qquad t_2(S)=(S,\pi_{\rm tr},0). \] Every assertion of Theorem~\ref{c:k3-gate} is also equivalent to \[ \bigwedge^{23-\rho}t_2(S)=0. \] Equivalently, the alternating sum of the products $(\pi_{\rm tr})_{a,\,23-\rho+\sigma(a)}$, over $\sigma\in S_{23-\rho}$, vanishes on $S^{2(23-\rho)}$. For Picard rank $1$ this is a test on $44$ factors. This smaller correspondence uses divisor classes outside the narrow requested ring; its factor count therefore does not contradict the unconditional narrow-ring result through $45$ factors.
status: Proved smaller equivalent vanishing test; general vanishing unresolved
notes: Picard rank1 gives44 factors with divisor projectors outside the narrow ring; narrow first determinant remains on46 factors.

statement: The unconditional K3 range: For every projective complex K3 surface with its Beauville--Voisin class, the requested relations hold in every power $S^k$ with $k\leq45$. More generally they hold in normalized degree $d$ of every $S^k$ whenever \[ \min(d,k-d)\leq22, \] where normalized degree $d$ means Chow codimension $2d$. In this range no finite-dimensionality assumption is required.
status: Proved
notes: First unproved universal determinant occurs at k46,d23; codimension is2d.

statement: An explicit genus-three failure: Let $C/\C$ be the plane quartic $X^4+Y^4=Z^4$, and take $o=(0:1:1)$. Its modified diagonal $M_o$ vanishes in every Weil cohomology, but \[ M_o\ne0\quad\hbox{in }\CH^2(C^3)_\Q. \] Thus the cohomological relation in Proposition~\ref{c:modified-diagonal} fails in rational Chow groups for this completely specified genus-three pointed curve.
status: Proved counterexample
notes: Smooth genus three; Bloch proves Sigma non-torsion modulo algebraic equivalence; exact odd sum-map pushforward is 3 Sigma in Chow.

statement: A gauged special bivariant system: Over a characteristic-zero field $L$, a special bivariant system assigns to every finite set $I$ a finite-dimensional graded-commutative algebra $A(I)$, with $A(\varnothing)=L$, a trace $\kappa_I$ of degree $-D|I|$, and a perfect trace pairing. For a map $\alpha:I\to J$ it assigns \[ \alpha^*:A(I)\longrightarrow A(J),\qquad \alpha_*:A(J)\longrightarrow A(I). \] The first is a unital graded algebra homomorphism; the second has degree $D(|I|-|J|)$. Pullbacks compose covariantly in maps of indexing sets, pushforwards contravariantly, and \[ \kappa_I(\alpha_*x\,a)=\kappa_J(x\,\alpha^*a),\qquad \alpha_*(x\alpha^*a)=\alpha_*x\,a. \] For disjoint unions the exterior-product maps $A(I)\otimes A(J)\to A(I\amalg J)$ are isomorphisms compatible with associativity, units, traces, and the Koszul symmetry. These maps are compatible with pullback and pushforward. The exchange axiom is base change for product squares (a projection pulled back by a map on the other factor); arbitrary self-intersection squares are not included. The gauge is the chosen trace, not a quotient up to multiplication by a scalar. A morphism in the bivariant category from $A$ to $B$ is a pair $(f^*,f_*)$, with $f^*:B\to A$ a unital graded algebra map and $f_*:A\to B$ its trace adjoint. On powers these maps are tensor powers and satisfy the corresponding pullback and pushforward compatibilities. The adjoint need not preserve the unit.
status: Definition, with the corrected exchange axiom
notes: Unrestricted Cartesian base change excluded explicitly.

statement: C.2: equivalence and the exchange axiom: Special gauged bivariant systems are equivalent to finite-dimensional graded-commutative Frobenius algebras of even top degree, with bivariant adjoint morphisms. The functor taking a system to its one-factor algebra and diagonal coevaluation is fully faithful. For a smooth projective connected variety, $I\mapsto H^*(X^I)$ satisfies these axioms. Correspondence composition defined by these axioms is associative and has the diagonal as identity.
status: Proved, with the category specified above
notes: Includes full faithfulness, Weil cohomology example, and associativity.

statement: The R7 hypotheses used in this Part: We checked the proof in the supplied reading, \S\S2.1--2.3, against 12:150--158. The conditional construction there is not a construction of a faithful realization on all Chow motives: it first quotients by the chosen homological equivalence, assumes its equality with numerical equivalence and the stated positivity, and then takes the semisimple envelope. Our Chow assertions above do not use this conditional passage. In particular it cannot be used to kill the homologically zero K3 determinant. The sign correction is forced by the cross-product formula: interchanging a class of degree $a$ with one of degree $b$ multiplies it by $(-1)^{ab}$. Thus the original realization is symmetric into graded vector spaces with that commutativity constraint. This is the convention used in our Frobenius equivalence. A level filtration by thick subcategories yields a direct-sum level decomposition only when the ambient category is semisimple; then we group the simple constituents according to their least allowed twist. Thickness alone gives no splitting of extensions. The geometric level definition of C.4 therefore does not assert a canonical splitting or identify itself with coniveau. The internal-Hom error of 12:156 already occurs in the semisimple effective Tate category with objects finite sums of $\Q(-a)$, $a\geq0$. For every effective $Z$, \[ \Hom(Z\otimes\Q(-1),\Q)=0. \] Hence the effective internal Hom from $\Q(-1)$ to $\Q$ is the zero object. After adjoining all Tate twists the corresponding internal Hom is $\Q(1)$, which is nonzero. Thus effective internal Homs need not be preserved by Tate inversion. In a rigid tensor category the valid identity is \[ \underline{\Hom}(M,N(-i)) =M^\vee\otimes N(-i) =M^*\otimes N, \qquad M^*=M^\vee(-i). \] Evaluation and coevaluation give these isomorphisms and their inverse maps. Merely postulating the effective object $M^*$ without the duality identities does not prove them. These checks confirm precisely the restrictions of R7 needed here.
status: Used and rechecked, with its internal-Hom counterexample confirmed
notes: No homological realization faithfulness on Chow motives inferred from the conditional construction.

statement: The invariant-centre identity: For a pro-reductive group $G$ over a characteristic-zero field, \[ \Hom_G(\mathbf1,\Lie G)=(\Lie G)^G=\Lie Z(G). \] If $G$ is connected, the map from its centre to its abelianization induces an isomorphism on Lie algebras. If $G^\circ$ has protorus abelianization $S$ and $\Gamma=G/G^\circ$, then \[ (\Lie G)^G=(\Lie S)^\Gamma. \] The invariant condition under $\Gamma$ cannot be discarded.
status: Proved
notes: Pro-reductive inverse-limit version included.

statement: Lead C3 with its arithmetic action: Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, embedded in $\C$, and let $K_0$ be the algebraic closure of $\Q$ in $K$. Suppose that the geometric connected motivic group is pro-reductive, that its maximal protorus quotient is the full Serre protorus $S$, and that the action of $\Gal(\overline K/K)$ on this quotient is the usual action through $\Gal(\overline\Q/K_0)$. If $E$ is the largest CM subfield of $K_0$, then \[ \dim_\Q (\Lie G)^G= \begin{cases}1+[E:\Q]/2,&E\text{ exists},\\1,&K_0\text{ has no CM subfield}. \end{cases} \] These hypotheses hold for the full category of motivated motives of abelian type, including Artin motives. The conclusion concerns the full arithmetic adjoint invariants; the centre of the geometric connected group alone is generally an infinite-dimensional pro-vector space.
status: Proved under the stated Serre-quotient hypothesis
notes: Geometric centre alone is generally infinite-dimensional.

statement: The finite-field analytic/algebraic distinction: Let $E/\F_5$ have equation $y^2=x^3-x$. It is smooth since its discriminant $64$ is nonzero modulo $5$. It has eight rational points, so geometric Frobenius has polynomial $T^2+2T+5$ on $H^1$ and eigenvalues $\pi=-1+2i$, $\bar\pi=-1-2i$. Its algebraic Frobenius torus is \[ T=\operatorname{Res}_{\Q(i)/\Q}\Gm, \qquad\dim T=2. \] Indeed the two primes of $\Q(i)$ above $5$ give valuations $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ on $(\pi,\bar\pi)$; hence $\pi^a\bar\pi^b=1$ implies $a=b=0$. There is consequently no character cutting out a proper algebraic subgroup containing Frobenius. The adjoint action of $T$ is trivial, so its whole Lie algebra is algebraic, but it is two-dimensional. On the other hand, for $\ell=3$ a suitable positive power of $\pi$ belongs to $1+3\Z_3[i]$. The analytic closure of the cyclic Frobenius subgroup has Lie algebra $\Q_3\log(\pi^N)$, of dimension one. The logarithm is nonzero because $\pi$ is not a root of unity. This is the distinction made by Serre in his letter of 8 September 1964, printed p.~202 of \citet{c_grothendieckserre}. Thus ``tout'' on 12:59 is valid for the adjoint Lie algebra of a commutative algebraic motivic band, as in the finite-field category under the Tate hypotheses of Part A; the accompanying identification with a single $\Q(0)$ does not describe that algebraic Lie object. Treating an analytic one-dimensional image as the motivic Lie algebra is an error, not an unconditional proof of a finite-field motivic assertion.
status: Proved counterexample to the one-dimensional algebraic reading
notes: Tout valid for commutative band; single Q(0) invalid for algebraic Lie interpretation.

statement: The level convention of 12:111--115: We fix $\ell$ invertible on the base and use $\Q_\ell(1)$ of weight $-2$. In the dimension-normalized convention, a special lisse sheaf of weight $r\geq0$ is a lisse subquotient of $R^rg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective morphism $g$ of relative dimension $r$. This includes the inserted dimension clause on 12:111; the transcription marks its following qualifier as uncertain. ``Strictly special'' means a direct summand, as clarified in 12:113. We explicitly call the version without a restriction on the relative dimension the broader convention. Over a field the two conventions agree, by the cut-and-pairing argument in Lemma~\ref{c:proper-level}; Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound} first uses the dimension-normalized convention, and Proposition~\ref{c:broader-coefficients} removes that clause for the general polygon and for the requested margin bound. Effective admissibility means that, after a finite stratification and the finite extensions allowed in 12:111, there is a finite filtration by extensions by zero of such sheaves. A sheaf has levels at most $\nu$ if these pieces may be chosen as $V(-a)$ with $a\geq0$, where $V$ is special of weight $r\leq\nu$. The simultaneous condition of weights in $\Phi$ requires the same pieces to satisfy $r+2a\in\Phi$. This is the geometric generation definition in 12:112; it is not simply a definition in terms of the eigenvalue weights, and it is not automatically the coniveau filtration.
status: Definition, checked against 12:111--115
notes: Not identified with a numerical weight bound or coniveau.

statement: C.4: the general $n-1$ bound is false: In the generality requested in the prompt, the bound \[ \operatorname{level}(R^if_*F)_{\bar y} \leq\min\{i,d_y(f)-1\}+j \] is false. Take $f:E\to\Spec\F_5$ for the elliptic curve in Example~\ref{c:finite-field-lie}, $F=\Q_\ell$, $j=0$, $i=1$, and any $\ell\ne5$. Then $d_y(f)=1$ and the right side is zero, whereas $H^1(E_{\overline\F_5},\Q_\ell)$ has level exactly one.
status: Refuted, with the precise manuscript correction
notes: Manuscript box is min(i,n)+j; margin has extra relative-dimension condition.

statement: Sharp elementary cases: If $f:X\to\Spec k$ is smooth projective of dimension $n$ and $F=\Q_\ell$, then $H^i(X)$ is pure of weight $i$ over a finite field and has level at most $\min(i,2n-i)$. Over a smooth pair $(Y,D)$ with a strict normal-crossing divisor and open immersion $j:Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow Y$, if $r$ branches meet at a geometric point $\bar y$, then \[ (R^ij_*\Q_\ell)_{\bar y}\simeq \bigwedge^i\bigl(\Q_\ell(-1)^r\bigr). \] It vanishes for $i>r$ and, when nonzero, has weight $2i$ and level zero. If a strictly special lisse sheaf extends across this pair, the projection formula tensors this description with its stalk.
status: Proved in the stated cases
notes: Universal replacement and margin now proved in c:general-level-bound under its explicit scope.

statement: The local dimension on 12:120: For a finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of universally catenary noetherian schemes we use \[ d_y(f)=\sup_{\substack{x\in X\\ f(x)\text{ generalizes }y}} \left\{\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(f(x))}k(x) +\dim\overline{\{f(x)\}}^{\,\Spec\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\right\}. \] The closure in the second summand is taken in the local base. This is the dimension function, normalized to be zero at $y$, pulled back to $X$. It is the formula visible in the supplied transcription, whose notation for the local spectrum is uncertain. It measures local source dimension, not maximum fibre dimension: for $\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec R$ with $R$ a discrete valuation ring and $y$ its closed point it equals $1$, although all nonempty fibres have dimension zero. After an equidimensional localization of the source and a compactification, its maximum is the local dimension of that compactification. Regular alterations preserve this maximum. The dimension-function convention and the corresponding local cohomological interpretation are made precise in \citet[\S1.1.1 and Corollary 1.2.2]{c_pillonistroh2014}.
status: Definition, with the punctured-trait correction verified
notes: Not the Krull dimension of a nonproper localized source.

statement: Proper cohomology with simultaneous geometric bounds: Let $Z$ be proper of dimension at most $d$ over a field $k$, and let $a\geq0$. After the finite field extensions allowed in the admissibility definition, $H^a(Z_{\bar k},\Q_\ell)$ has a finite filtration by subquotients of special objects $V_r(-t)$ satisfying \[ t\geq\max(0,a-d),\qquad r\geq0,\qquad r+2t\leq a. \] In particular its weights are at most $a$ and its geometric levels are at most $\min(a,2d-a)$. A negative upper level bound means the object is zero. These are geometric generation assertions, not deductions from a Hodge polygon.
status: Proved
notes: Galois-quotient alteration and dimension induction preserve simultaneous bounds.

statement: Corrected bounds and the margin question: Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, with $X$ regular and $X,Y$ of finite type over $\Z[1/\ell]$ or over a field of characteristic different from $\ell$. Fix $y\in Y$ and put $n=d_y(f)$. Let $F$ be strictly special of weight $j$, in the dimension-normalized sense of the insertion on 12:111: it is a direct summand of $R^jg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective $g$ of relative dimension $j$. Set $\epsilon=1$ if no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, and set $\epsilon=0$ otherwise. Put \[ L=\max(0,i-n+\epsilon),\qquad U=\min(i,n)+j. \] The stalk $(R^if_*F)_{\bar y}$ is effectively admissible, with a filtration into pieces of weights $w$ and levels bounded simultaneously by \begin{equation} 2L\leq w\leq2U, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq\min\{w-2L,\,2U-w\}. \end{equation} Consequently \[ \operatorname{weight}\leq2\min(i,n)+2j, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq \begin{cases} \min(i,2n-i)+j,&\epsilon=0,\\ \min(i,2n-1-i)+j,&\epsilon=1. \end{cases} \] For an open immersion at a boundary point, $\epsilon=1$. The condition that $f$ have relative dimension at most $n-1$ near $y$ also implies $\epsilon=1$. Hence the margin's replacement by $n-1$ is valid with its stated extra condition, since $\min(i,2n-1-i)\leq\min(i,n-1)$. Without that condition the corrected general bound is at most $\min(i,n)+j$, and Proposition~\ref{c:level-counterexample} prevents replacing $n$ by $n-1$ universally.
status: Proved in the stated arithmetic finite-type setting
notes: Level min(i,2n-i)+j; margin/open-boundary level min(i,2n-1-i)+j; weight <=2min(i,n)+2j.

statement: Removing the dimension clause from the coefficient: Keep the finite-type hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound}, but suppose only that $F$ is a direct summand of $R^jg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective $g:Z\to X$ of arbitrary relative dimension. Put $n=d_y(f)$ and $L_0=\max(0,i-n)$, $U=\min(i,n)+j$. Then the simultaneous bounds \[ 2L_0\leq w\leq2U,\qquad \operatorname{level}\leq\min(w-2L_0,2U-w) \] still hold. In particular the general level bound is $\min(i,2n-i)+j$. If no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, there is also the bound \[ \operatorname{level}\leq\min(i,n-1)+j. \] Consequently the requested weight bound and the manuscript's margin bound hold in this broader convention as well. The stronger margin polygon with $L_0$ replaced by $\max(0,i-n+1)$ remains covered by Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound} in its dimension-normalized convention.
status: Proved
notes: General level min(i,2n-i)+j and margin level min(i,n-1)+j. Stronger reflected margin polygon retains the normalized presentation in this proof.

statement: Optimality and the limit of the word sharp: For constant coefficients the preceding upper weight and level bounds are attained for every nonnegative degree in the indicated nonzero ranges. The general and margin level bounds remain optimal after adding $j$. The coefficient $2j$ in the universal weight envelope cannot be replaced by $j$: for every $j\geq0$ there is a strictly special weight-$j$ example with $n=i=1$ whose $R^1$ boundary stalk is pure of weight $2j+2$.
status: Proved optimality in the stated senses
notes: For j>0 weight envelope is attained in interior degrees. Top endpoint improved to2n+j; lower endpoint has exact local-invariant-cycle gate.

statement: The top degree and its sharper weight: In the finite-type setting of Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound}, let $F$ be any lisse $\Q_\ell$-sheaf. Then $(R^if_*F)_{\bar y}=0$ for $i>2n$. If no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, it vanishes already for $i>2n-1$. If $k(y)$ is finite and $F$ is pure of weight $j$, the degree-$2n$ stalk is pure of weight $2n+j$ when nonzero. This endpoint is attained by $\mathbb P^n\to\Spec\F_q$ with constant coefficient $H^j(E^j)$ for an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$. These assertions do not require the dimension-normalized presentation of $F$.
status: Proved
notes: Any lisse coefficient for vanishing; pure weight-j coefficient at a finite-field point for top weight; no dimension-j normalization required.

statement: An improved bound in degree zero: Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type over $\Z[1/\ell]$ or over a finite field of characteristic different from $\ell$, with $X$ regular, and let $y\in Y$ have finite residue field. Let $F$ be strictly special of weight $j\geq0$, in either convention of Definition~\ref{c:level-def}. Put \[ b(0)=0,\qquad b(1)=1,\qquad b(j)=2j-2\quad(j\geq2). \] Then the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on $(f_*F)_{\bar y}$ have weights at most $b(j)$. In particular, the expected bound $j$ holds for $j\leq2$. The assertion about weights does not replace the geometric level definition or assert a corresponding smaller level.
status: Proved; optimality for general coefficients of weight at least three remains unresolved
notes: General i0 endpoint now settled for j<=2. Does not assert optimality for j>=3 or a sharper geometric level.

statement: The first remaining lower-endpoint case: Let $Z$ be a smooth projective threefold over a mixed-characteristic local field with a projective strictly semistable model, and $\ell\ne p$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $H^3(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}$ has weights at most $3$; \item $N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_4H^3\to \operatorname{Gr}^W_2H^3(-1)$ is injective; \item the weight--monodromy conjecture holds for $H^3(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$. \end{enumerate} Here the weight filtration $W$ is supplied by the weight spectral sequence, and the weight--monodromy statement means that $N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_{3+r}\to \operatorname{Gr}^W_{3-r}(-r)$ is an isomorphism for every $r\geq0$.
status: Proved equivalence for this case; the stated monodromy map remains unresolved in general
notes: First residual normalized trait case j3; only possible excess weight4 remains.

statement: The exact surface-pairing obstruction in dimension three: Let $\mathcal X$ be a projective strictly semistable model of a smooth projective threefold $X$ over a mixed-characteristic local field with finite residue field $k$, and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Write $Y^{(r)}$ for the disjoint union, over $\bar k$, of the $r$-fold intersections of distinct components of its special fibre. All cohomology below has coefficients $\Q_\ell$. Put \[ A=H^2(Y^{(1)}),\quad U=H^2(Y^{(2)}),\quad B=H^0(Y^{(3)})(-1),\quad Z=H^0(Y^{(4)})(-1). \] Use the signed restriction and Gysin maps of the weight spectral sequence, and define \[ \begin{split} R&=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\rho_A:A\longrightarrow U\bigr),\\ K_0&=R\cap\gamma_B \ker\bigl(\rho_B:B\longrightarrow Z\bigr),\\ b(u,v)&=\sum_{S\subset Y^{(2)}}\operatorname{Tr}_S(u_Sv_S) \ \in\Q_\ell(-2). \end{split} \] Then $K_0\subset\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)$, and there is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism \begin{equation} \ker\!\left( N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_4H^3(X_{\bar K})(1) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}^W_2H^3(X_{\bar K}) \right) \simeq \frac{\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)}{K_0}. \end{equation} Consequently the first remaining C.4 endpoint assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the induced form on $R/K_0$. Choose a relatively ample class $L$. The same assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the surface intersection form on \begin{equation} R_{\rm prim} =R\cap \ker\bigl( L:H^2(Y^{(2)})\longrightarrow H^4(Y^{(2)})(1) \bigr). \end{equation} In particular the remaining condition involves only a primitive restriction image in the degree-two cohomology of the double-intersection surfaces. It does not require the unknown nondegeneracy of an additional Gysin image.
status: Proved reduction; the remaining primitive pairing is unresolved
notes: Kernel is rad(R)/(R intersect gamma ker rho). The primitive Gysin condition is automatic by known degree-two monodromy. No general vanishing asserted.

statement: Removing the rational divisor restriction image: Retain the notation of Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel}. Let $N_r=\operatorname{NS}(Y^{(r)})_\Q$ for $r=1,2$, and let $\rho_{\rm NS}:N_1\to N_2$ be signed restriction. Define the rational space \[ D_{\rm prim}= \operatorname{im}(\rho_{\rm NS})\cap \ker\!\left( N_2\longrightarrow \bigoplus_{S\subset Y^{(2)}}\Q,\quad (d_S)_S\longmapsto(\deg(L_Sd_S))_S \right). \] We regard $D_{\rm prim}\otimes\Q_\ell(-1)$ as a subspace of $R_{\rm prim}$ by the divisor cycle map. Then \[ R_{\rm prim} =\bigl(D_{\rm prim}\otimes\Q_\ell(-1)\bigr) \mathbin{\perp}R_{\rm rem}, \qquad R_{\rm rem}= R_{\rm prim}\cap \bigl(D_{\rm prim}\otimes\Q_\ell(-1)\bigr)^\perp . \] The first summand has a nondegenerate negative-definite rational intersection form. Consequently the remaining threefold assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the form on $R_{\rm rem}$. If the divisor Tate conjecture holds for every smooth projective surface over finite fields of the residue characteristic, let $T_r\subset H^2(Y^{(r)})$ be the Frobenius spectral summand whose eigenvalues are not $|k|$ times roots of unity. Then \[ R_{\rm rem}=\rho_A(T_1)\subset T_2. \] Thus, under that separate surface-Tate hypothesis, the remaining pairing is entirely on the image of the transcendental degree-two spectral summand.
status: Proved unconditional splitting; the spectral identification uses surface Tate
notes: Only rational divisor preimages are removed unconditionally. Under the separate surface-Tate hypothesis the remainder is rho(T1) in T2. No full Frobenius semisimplicity or geometric positivity transfer is inferred.

statement: The geometric content not removed by the pairing criterion: The radical formula is an exact identification of the existing kernel. The primitive criterion additionally removes the nonprimitive Lefschetz pieces and the Gysin-image condition. It does not prove the resulting nondegeneracy. In particular, containment of a $\Q_\ell$-subspace in the span of divisor classes does not allow one to apply rational Hodge-index positivity to that subspace without establishing its rational origin. For example, over $\Q_5$, choose $\iota^2=-1$ with $\iota\equiv2\pmod5$. The line $\Q_5(1,\iota)$ is isotropic for $-x^2-y^2$ although this form is negative definite over $\Q$. It is stable under the scalar Frobenius $2I$. This is a counterexample to that linear-algebra inference, not a geometric counterexample to weight--monodromy. For the same reason, an isomorphism of a stratum motive with an abelian motive would not alone identify its geometric primitive form with a positive polarization. The conditional image-projector and positivity inputs in \citet[Theorem~0.4 and \S\S4.1--4.3]{c_msaito2003positivity} remain separate hypotheses. We have not silently supplied either input from Frobenius purity or from the 2026 theorem for CM abelian varieties. The corresponding warning is explicit in \citet[submitted version, Remark~4.10 and footnote~3, p.~14]{DMilne2002Polarizations}: equality of motive categories under a Tate hypothesis does not by itself transfer the positivity of the geometric forms. The published-version Theorem~3.3 and Corollary~3.4 concern abelian varieties.
status: Proved scope clarification; the primitive nondegeneracy is open
notes: The negative rational form may have isotropic Q_l subspaces without rational origin. CM Hodge and abstract abelian-motive isomorphisms do not supply arbitrary geometric polarization compatibility.

statement: A target-only sufficient positivity hypothesis: Retain the strictly semistable threefold setting and fixed $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ of Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel}, and put $V=Y^{(1)}$, $S=Y^{(2)}$. After a finite extension of the finite residue field, we may suppose that the geometric components are individually defined. Assume the Hodge standard conjecture $I(S\times S,L\boxplus L)$ and equality of $\ell$-homological and numerical equivalence for rational cycles on $V\times S$. Here the first assumption includes the products of distinct surface components. Then the primitive restriction image $R_{\rm prim}$ has nondegenerate intersection pairing. Consequently weight--monodromy holds on $H^3$ of the generic threefold. No Lefschetz standard conjecture on $V$ is required in this sufficient package. Alternatively, suppose that for each component $V_i$ an inverse to \[ L_i:H^2(V_i)\longrightarrow H^4(V_i)(1) \] is induced by an algebraic correspondence. Choose smooth ample surfaces $j_i:T_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ with classes $m_iL_i$, and put $T=\coprod_iT_i$. Then the same conclusion follows from $I(S\times S,L\boxplus L)$ and homological equals numerical equivalence on $T\times S$. Only the relevant homogeneous degree-two mixed trace pairings are needed in either formulation; full equality of the two equivalences on the displayed products is a sufficient hypothesis.
status: Proved conditional refinement; the general primitive pairing remains unresolved
notes: I(SxS)+D(VxS) needs no source B or source semisimplicity. A supplied B2(V) replaces mixed VxS by TxS for ample surfaces T. Modified full-H2 pairing, actual primitive intersection and finite-Q corner are explicit.

statement: A simple-spectrum substitute for target positivity: We keep the threefold semistable notation of Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel}. After fixing a finite residue field $\F_q$ over which all the components and the chosen ample classes are defined, put \[ V=Y^{(1)},\qquad S=Y^{(2)},\qquad f=\rho:H^2(V,\Q_\ell)\longrightarrow H^2(S,\Q_\ell), \qquad P=H^2(S,\Q_\ell)_{\rm prim}. \] Here primitivity is imposed separately on each surface component, using the restrictions of the fixed ample class. Assume that numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree on $V\times S$, and that the characteristic polynomial of geometric Frobenius on the entire space $P$ is squarefree. Then the cup-product pairing on \[ \operatorname{im}(f)\cap P \] is nondegenerate. Consequently the first threefold monodromy condition in Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel} holds. The squarefreeness condition concerns the union of all surface components, including possible coincidences between their eigenvalues. It is not enough to impose squarefreeness separately on each component. We do not assume the standard conjecture of Hodge type on $S\times S$, or a semisimplicity statement for the source motive. The proof uses algebraic projectors that are idempotent on cohomology; it does not require idempotence modulo rational equivalence.
status: Proved sufficient condition; the universal threefold gate remains open
notes: All components and ample classes are defined over the fixed finite residue field before imposing squarefreeness. No D(SxS), source semisimplicity, or Chow-idempotent lift used. Actual im(f) intersection P obtained, not im(pf).; Squarefreeness is global across the disjoint union and can fail after taking Frobenius powers. No transfer removes either retained hypothesis.

statement: Limits of the simple-spectrum criterion: The proposition replaces the full target positivity hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-target-positivity} by one directly testable condition on a Frobenius characteristic polynomial. It retains the mixed numerical-equals-homological hypothesis needed to obtain the algebraic kernel and image projectors. Neither that hypothesis nor the squarefreeness of the primitive target spectrum has been proved for all semistable threefolds. Eigenvalues on different components can coincide, and distinct eigenvalues can become equal after a finite residue-field extension. We have not produced an alteration or other transfer that removes these conditions. Thus this is a sufficient subcase, not movement on the general C.4 assertion.
status: Proved scope clarification; no unconditional reduction of the universal gate
notes: Squarefreeness is global across the disjoint union and can fail after taking Frobenius powers. No transfer removes either retained hypothesis.

statement: A finite exterior-power test for monodromy purity: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional mixed Frobenius module over $\Q_\ell$, with integral weights and a nilpotent operator $N:V\to V(-1)$. Fix an integer $m$. We use geometric Frobenius $\phi$ and $\phi N\phi^{-1}=q^{-1}N$. Suppose \[ \sum_w w\dim V_w=m\dim V, \] where $V=\bigoplus_wV_w$ is the decomposition by Frobenius weights; Frobenius need not be semisimple. Let $h$ be the largest length of a Jordan string of $N$, with $h=0$ if $V=0$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $V$ is pure of weight $m$ in the weight--monodromy sense; \item for every $1\leq r\leq h$, all weights of $\ker(N:\bigwedge^r V\to\bigwedge^r V(-1))$ are at most $rm$. \end{enumerate} Here the exterior power is the ordinary exterior power of vector spaces, and $N$ acts on it as a derivation. The determinant hypothesis holds in particular when $V$ has a nondegenerate Frobenius-equivariant pairing $V\otimes V\to\Q_\ell(-m)$.
status: Proved
notes: No Frobenius semisimplicity is required. Test through the largest N-string length; no novelty or universal-gate closure claimed.

statement: The universal trait endpoint and weight--monodromy: Fix a residue characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. We consider finite extensions $K/\Q_p$, with finite residue field, and geometric $\ell$-adic cohomology. The following universal assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Weight--monodromy holds for $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for every smooth projective $Z/K$ and every $j\geq0$. \item For every smooth projective $j$-fold $Z/K$, $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}$ has weights at most $j$. \item The assertion in (2) holds for the generic fibres of projective strictly semistable models over $\mathcal O_K$. \end{enumerate} In (2) the stated space is the closed geometric stalk of $u_*H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for the open immersion $u:\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec\mathcal O_K$. Thus it is exactly the dimension-normalized, degree-zero trait endpoint. For an individual $j$-fold, after a finite extension making its inertia action unipotent, it suffices to test the bound $rj$ on $\ker N$ in $\bigwedge^r H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for $1\leq r\leq j+1$. Each such test is a direct-summand test in the middle cohomology $H^{rj}(Z^r_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$. A failure of weight--monodromy therefore yields a trait-endpoint failure on one of these powers, or on a projective semistable alteration of that power.
status: Proved equivalence; the universal assertions remain unresolved
notes: For a j-fold the witness uses r<=j+1 and middle H^(rj)(X^r). Separate L_r extensions avoid a false common-model base-change step. Ordinary exterior projector has explicit Koszul sign. Trait scope retained.

statement: One exterior test can miss a failure: Take $K=\Q_2$, $\ell=3$, $q=2$, and an unramified Weil representation over $\Q_3$ with basis $u_6,v_4,x_4,y_2$, subscripts denoting weights. Put \[ \phi=\operatorname{diag}(8,4,4,2),\qquad N(u_6)=v_4,\quad N(x_4)=y_2,\quad N(v_4)=N(y_2)=0. \] Its two string centres are $5$ and $3$, so it is not weight--monodromy pure of weight $4$. Nevertheless its determinant has weight $16=4\dim V$ and $\ker N=\langle v_4,y_2\rangle$ has weights at most $4$. It even has the nondegenerate symmetric pairing into $\Q_\ell(-4)$ specified by \[ \langle u_6,y_2\rangle=1,\qquad \langle v_4,x_4\rangle=-1 \] and symmetric counterparts, all other entries being zero. The identities $\phi N\phi^{-1}=2^{-1}N$, $N^{\mathsf T}Q+QN=0$, and $\phi^{\mathsf T}Q\phi=2^4Q$ are immediate matrix identities. In $\bigwedge^2V$, the nonzero vector $u_6\wedge v_4$ is killed by $N$ and has weight $10>8$. The second exterior test detects the failure. The exact rational-matrix certificate \path{code/part_c/check_c4_exterior_witness.py} and its companion \path{code/part_c/check_c4_exterior_witness_output.json} verify these identities and the exterior-power calculation. This is a counterexample only to the proposed linear-algebra implication from the single invariant bound and self-duality. It is not a smooth projective fourfold or a counterexample to geometric weight--monodromy.
status: Proved formal counterexample; no geometric realization asserted
notes: K=Q2, ell=3, weights6,4,4,2, two length2 strings of centres5 and3. Exact code and JSON supplied; not a counterexample to geometric WM.

statement: Scope of the trait criterion: The theorem identifies the universal middle-degree trait endpoint with weight--monodromy and gives a finite power witness to a failure. It does not prove either universal assertion. Its bound $r\leq j+1$ uses the actual nonnegative cohomological degree $j$; it is not a bound in terms of the weight of an arbitrary Tate-twisted motive. The finite inertia quotient can remove a vector from the invariants at the original place, which is why the witness is taken after a finite semistable extension. All local fields are quantified in the universal assertion, so this extension is permitted. The argument concerns the stated traits. For a general morphism in C.4, the component and curve-selection argument in Proposition~\ref{c:improved-zero-weight} is an additional required transfer; no general sheaf bound is inferred merely by naming the trait equivalence.
status: Proved scope clarification; universal C.4 remains incomplete
notes: r<=j+1 uses actual effective cohomological degree, not arbitrary Tate-twisted weight. Finite inertia may hide original-place witnesses. General f requires the separately proved curve-selection transfer.

statement: The lower-endpoint gate over a trait: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field $k$, fraction field $K$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$. Let $\mathcal Z/R$ be regular, proper, flat and generically smooth, with generic fibre $Z$. For $u:\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec R$, the assertion that \[ (u_*H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell))_{\bar k} =H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K} \quad\text{has weights at most }j \] is equivalent to surjectivity of the specialization map \[ H^j(\mathcal Z_{\bar k},\Q_\ell) \longrightarrow H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}. \] Thus, when $\dim Z=j$, improving the universal $i=0$ coefficient bound from $2j$ to $j$ includes exactly this local invariant cycle assertion.
status: Proved exact equivalence; the general mixed-characteristic vanishing is not asserted
notes: General mixed-characteristic local-invariant-cycle gate remains; abelian-type trait coefficients now satisfy the upper weight-j endpoint unconditionally.

statement: The lower endpoint for abelian-type coefficients: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field of characteristic $p$, and let $\ell\ne p$. Suppose that $V$ is the $\ell$-adic realization of a pure weight-$j$ motive which, after a finite extension of $K$, is a direct summand of tensor constructions on the $H^1$ of abelian varieties, their duals and Tate twists. Finite-image Artin factors are allowed. Then the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on $V^{I_K}$ have weights at most $j$. In particular this holds for the local realizations of pure absolute-Hodge or motivated motives of abelian type over number fields. The bound is attained for good reduction.
status: Proved
notes: Settles the trait lower endpoint for abelian-type coefficients without the 2026 rationality theorem.

statement: The positive purity range: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a two-dimensional regular local ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and let $U=\Spec R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. Every abelian scheme over $U$ extends uniquely over $R$ if $p\notin\mathfrak m^p$. In particular the sufficient absolute ramification bound is $e\leq p-1$, including equality. More generally the same conclusion holds under the complete faithfully flat quotient condition of Vasiu--Zink Theorem 3. If an abelian variety over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has good reduction at every height-one prime, these conclusions apply to it. Equivalently, at each such prime one may use the prime-to-residue-characteristic unramifiedness test of the N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich criterion.
status: Known, with its application proved
notes: Improves sufficient e<p-1 to e<=p-1.

statement: An explicit abelian-surface counterexample at $p=2$: Let $k=\overline\F_2$ and \[ R=W(k)[[u,v]]/(2-uv),\qquad K=\operatorname{Frac}(R),\qquad \mathfrak m=(u,v). \] Consider the elliptic schemes \begin{align*} E_1:&\quad Y^2Z+(u+v^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3,\\ E_2:&\quad Y^2Z+(v+u^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3, \end{align*} with origins $[0:1:0]$, and put $A=E_1\times_R E_2$. The sections \[ P_v=[-v:1:v^3]\in E_1(R),\qquad P_u=[-u:1:u^3]\in E_2(R) \] have order two on the generic fibre. Let $C_K\subset A_K$ be the order-two subgroup generated by $(P_v,P_u)$, and define the abelian surface \[ B_K=A_K/C_K. \] Then $B_K$ has good reduction at every height-one prime of $R$, hence its $T_\ell$ is unramified at every height-one point of $S_\ell=\Spec R[1/\ell]$ for every prime $\ell$, but it does not extend to an abelian scheme over $R$. The schematic closure of $C_K$ in $A$ is explicitly nonflat.
status: Proved refutation of the unrestricted criterion
notes: All polynomial identities checked over integers without inverting 2.

statement: What fails to extend: The abstract finite group $D_U$ already extends as $D$. It is its closed immersion into $A_U$, and consequently the exact sequence defining the isogeny, that cannot extend as a finite flat subgroup. Indeed finite locally free group schemes on a punctured regular local surface extend as objects by extending their coordinate bundles to reflexive modules, which are free in dimension two; multiplication and comultiplication extend by Hartogs. Exactness and closed-immersion conditions need not survive. This is the precise content of the finite-subgroup reduction in R6, rather than a failure to extend the abstract group. The source proof of Vasiu--Zink Lemma 27 reverses the Cartier-dual arrows in its printed embedding sentence; our displayed maps avoid that typing error. Lead C5 is therefore valid as an identification of the extension obstruction, while the unrestricted good-reduction claim is false.
status: Proved clarification
notes: Corrects ambiguity in the finite-subgroup reduction and a dual-arrow typo in Vasiu-Zink Lemma27.

statement: The degree-one and semistable abelian-type cases: Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place of residue characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$. For $M=h^1(A)$, unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell$ and is equivalent to good reduction of $A$. It follows for every tensor construction and motivated summand of abelian varieties already having good reduction at $v$. More generally suppose that $A/K$ has semistable reduction at $v$, that its Galois representations take values in its Mumford--Tate group $G$ over $K$, and that a motivated abelian-type object $M$ in the category it generates corresponds to a rational representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Then unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell\ne p$. The same conclusion holds for potentially CM motives without a semistability assumption.
status: Proved in the stated cases
notes: The elementary cases are now subsumed by c:ell-independence-abelian; retained to isolate the older SGA7/Kisin-Zhou inputs.

statement: A generator with potentially good reduction: Let $M$ be a rational motive of abelian type over a number field $K$, in either the absolute-Hodge or motivated category. Let $v$ have residue characteristic $p$. If $M_{\ell_0}$ is potentially unramified at $v$ for one $\ell_0\ne p$, then, after a finite Galois extension $E/K$, the object $M_E$ belongs to the tensor category generated by finitely many abelian varieties over $E$ which have good reduction at every place above $v$.
status: Proved
notes: Descent via B0 factors; common MT group has finite derived kernel; all places above v retained.

statement:

statement: The exact role of the new input: The proof does not apply N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich to an arbitrary original generator: such a generator need not have good reduction when its summand is unramified. Lemma~\ref{c:potentially-good-generator} changes the generator and proves its potential good reduction. The finite descent action is then recovered over $K$ by the common trace pairing. Since \eqref{c:inertia-graph-lefschetz} is Lefschetz, the proof uses the rationality theorem alone; it does not use the CM Hodge theorem or assume algebraicity of the Hodge projector. statement: A purity reduction for homogeneous Chow motives: Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place with residue field of cardinality $q$, and $p$ its residue characteristic. Let $M=(X,e,m)$ be a rational Chow motive over $K$, where $X$ is smooth projective of dimension $d$ and the rational algebraic projector $e\in\CH^d(X\times_KX)_{\Q}$ acts only in cohomological degree $i$. Suppose that, for one prime $\ell_0\ne p$, the representation $M_{\ell_0}$ is unramified at $v$ and the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on it are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates have one common absolute value. Then $M_\ell$ is unramified at $v$ for every $\ell\ne p$. In particular, the asserted independence follows for such a motive if the weight--monodromy conjecture holds for $H^i(X_{\overline{K_v}},\Q_{\ell_0})$: its unramified direct summand $M_{\ell_0}$ is then pure of weight $i-2m$.
status: Proved conditional implication
notes: Ambient weight-monodromy at the one prime suffices; algebraic projector required.

statement: Exact scope of this reduction: For the full group $H^i(X)$, the purity assumption in the proposition is Serre's unramified-purity conjecture C7 \citep[\S2.3, printed p.~19-07]{c_serre1970local}. For a prescribed proper summand it is the corresponding \emph{motivic extension} of that condition; the literal original C7 must not be silently enlarged. The named weight--monodromy conjecture for the ambient cohomology is a sufficient alternative. The use of Saito's theorem requires an algebraic correspondence. It cannot be applied to an arbitrary absolute-Hodge or motivated projector without an additional comparison result. No converse to any of these named conjectures is proved here, and this proposition does not close the general-motive requirement in C.6.
status: Proved scope clarification; the general claim remains unresolved
notes: No converse to a named conjecture claimed.

statement: Surface and low-degree Chow constructions: Let $M$ be a pure rational Chow motive over a number field. Suppose that it is a homogeneous algebraic Chow summand of the cohomology of a finite product of smooth projective surfaces, or more generally belongs to the tensor constructions on supplied homogeneous algebraic Chow summands supported in degrees $0,1,2$ of smooth projective varieties, allowing finite sums, duals, Tate twists and homogeneous algebraic projectors. Then, at each finite place of residue characteristic $p$, unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ is independent of $\ell\ne p$.

statement: The precise conditional and categorical boundary: The hypothesis is a published, independently formulated independence-of-homological-equivalence conjecture over $\overline{\F}_p$, not a renamed version of C.6. The result proves only its implication to the stated C.6 assertion. It does not prove the converse: realizing an arbitrary finite-field correspondence as local monodromy of a number-field variety would require an additional geometric construction which is not supplied. The representative must be algebraic and homogeneous, but only its cohomological action must be idempotent. Inspecting the proof, idempotence is used on the realization and its $E_2$ graded pieces, never in the Chow group. No extension to an arbitrary absolute-Hodge, motivated, or numerical projector is inferred from Saito's algebraic-correspondence construction alone. The following theorem treats motivated projectors by an additional finite algebraic-and-Lefschetz construction. Thus this proposition gives a second exact sufficient hypothesis, alongside the purity reduction, but does not satisfy the requested general-motive proof or a two-way named-conjecture equivalence.

An arbitrary absolute-Hodge projector is not thereby proved motivated, and a numerical projector is not thereby supplied with a realization-compatible presentation. statement: Finite-prime approximation by a number-field motive: Let $K/\Q_p$ be finite, and let $M$ be a homogeneous rational motive over $K$ in either the algebraic homological category or Andr\'e's motivated category. For every nonempty finite set $\Sigma$ of primes different from $p$ there exist a number field $F\subset K$, a place $w$ of $F$ with $F_w=K$, and a homogeneous motive $M'$ of the same kind and weight over $F$, such that \[ H_\ell(M')|_{G_{F_w}}\simeq H_\ell(M) \qquad(\ell\in\Sigma) \] as representations of $G_K$, under the specified identification $F_w=K$. Consequently, universal independence of unramifiedness for these motives over number fields is equivalent to the same assertion over all finite extensions of $\Q_p$, for all $p$. The number-field approximation may depend on $\Sigma$.
status: Proved; a globalization reduction, not a proof of general independence
notes: Universal number-field unramifiedness independence is equivalent to the finite-p-adic-field assertion in these categories. Only a finite set of coefficient primes is preserved; no arbitrary absolute-Hodge spread is asserted.

statement: The remaining purity step in the analytic encoding: The preceding proposition removes number-field globalization as an additional obstruction once a pure algebraic or motivated local realization has been constructed. It does not turn an arbitrary compact rigid analytic motive into such a pure motive. In particular, the square-zero monodromy construction from \citet[Corollary~4.14]{c_bgv2024monodromy} still requires a pure local realization, or a proved reduction to finitely many pure local motives preserving the relevant unramifiedness flag. The finite-prime approximation is sufficient for the universal two-prime assertion; an approximation simultaneously preserving every coefficient prime has not been asserted.
status: Exact boundary; no converse to the finite-field conjecture is claimed
notes: Compact analytic or mixed algebraization does not supply a pure motive or a pure family preserving the ramification flag. No all-prime approximation or converse theorem is claimed.

statement: The remaining general-motive claim: Theorem~\ref{c:ell-independence-abelian} settles the whole abelian-type assertion, including its finite-inertia descent. The direct argument from an arbitrary original generator would still be invalid: $\bigwedge^2H^1(E)=\Q_\ell(-1)$ is unramified at a place of residue characteristic different from $\ell$, even when $E$ has bad reduction. The weak-lift lemma and the trace argument are what repair that inference. For Andr\'e motivated motives, Theorem~\ref{c:motivated-unramified-rank-reduction} supplies a second named sufficient hypothesis: independence of homological equivalence for rational cycles on all smooth projective varieties over $\overline{\F}_p$. It controls the monodromy ranks and the finite inertia action, but remains conditional on that finite-field conjecture. Corollary~\ref{c:motivated-abelian-strata-unramified} gives the stated unconditional geometric case only when all auxiliary strata have the required algebraic abelian-type presentations. Neither result proves a converse to the finite-field conjecture. For general motives, another precise named sufficient conjecture is Fontaine's motivic Weil--Deligne compatibility conjecture: \citet[\S2.4.3, Conjecture $C_{\mathrm{WD}}(X,m)$, p.~342, and its motivic formulation in \S2.4.7, pp.~344--345]{c_fontaine1994pst}. The motivic formulation is required to retain the specified projector; compatibility of an unlabelled ambient cohomology representation alone does not identify every prescribed summand. Write the local Weil--Deligne data as $(r_\ell,N_\ell)$, with $r_\ell$ of finite inertial image. On an open subgroup of inertia the actual action is $\exp(t_\ell(\tau)N_\ell)$, where the tame character has infinite image. Consequently \[ M_\ell\text{ is unramified at }v \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\ell=0\ \text{ and }\ r_\ell|_{I_v}=1. \] Both conditions are invariant under extension of coefficient fields and isomorphism of Weil--Deligne representations. Thus Fontaine's compatibility, which only requires isomorphism after common coefficient extension and not a chosen rational form, implies the requested independence. His weaker monodromy-graded character formulation in \S2.4.5 also suffices: the characters at the identity determine whether the monodromy filtration is concentrated in degree zero, equivalently $N=0$; after that, the finite inertia character detects triviality. This proves an implication, not the exact equivalence requested in the question. Algebraically, the representations trivial on a subgroup $J\subset G$ detect its closed normal closure, not the whole inertia representation. Even all tensor tests do not formally recover the nilpotent's Jordan type: in $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, both $E_{12}$ and $E_{12}+E_{23}$ act nontrivially in every nontrivial algebraic representation, since the differential's kernel is an ideal in the simple Lie algebra. Their ranks differ. The accompanying notes give compatible abstract Weil--Deligne pairs and a matrix certificate; no such pair is asserted to come from a global motive, and it is not a motivic counterexample. The theorem of \citet[Theorem 5.1]{c_commelin2019} concerns abelian motives and quasi-compatibility; by itself it does not supply finite-inertia traces for an arbitrary motive at a bad place. Similarly the $G$-valued expectation of \citet[Conjecture 1.1]{c_kisinzhou2025} is stronger than the asserted triviality test. A proof in the general motivic category, or an exact equivalence with a published named conjecture of precisely the required strength, remains an outstanding assertion, recorded separately from the now proved abelian-type theorem.
status: Unresolved in the general motivic category
notes: Abelian-type gap closed; general exact named-conjecture equivalence remains open in this work. Abstract SL3 examples certify only failure of a formal converse.

In particular $(\mathcal G^0)_\Q=T_{\mathfrak m} =\Res_{k/\Q}\Gm/\overline{E^+}^{\,\mathrm{Zar}}$. statement: Proved: all Weil numbers occur, with variable CM data: Let $\Gamma_q$ be the group of algebraic $p$-units whose complex conjugates have absolute value $q^{w/2}$ for some integer $w$. Every element of $\Gamma_q$ occurs as a Frobenius eigenvalue of the good reduction of a tensor CM motive over some number field at a place with residue field $\F_q$. Every integral weight-one member already occurs in $H^1$ of a CM abelian variety with such reduction. No single number field, finite modulus, or primitive CM type is asserted to work for all members.

statement: Proved: D.2(a) for abelian type and its general equivalent: For a motive $M$ of abelian type, in either category, \[ G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ\text{ is commutative} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M\in\CM(k). \] For arbitrary motives the same classification is equivalent to the following restricted Hodge-class assertion: \emph{CM comparison case of the absolute-Hodge (respectively motivated Hodge) conjecture.} If $G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ$ is commutative and $N$ is a CM abelian motive over $\overline k$, every rational Hodge morphism $H_B(M_{\overline k})\to H_B(N)$ is induced by an absolute Hodge (respectively motivated) correspondence. It is enough in this assertion to require one Hodge isomorphism to some such $N$ to lift. In the absolute-Hodge case this is a precise restriction of \citet[Conjecture 8.24]{c_delignehodge1982}, rather than a claim of equivalence with the unrestricted conjecture.

statement: Proved: finite-place kernel and fibre functors: There is a canonical identification \[ \Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K) \simeq \left\{(\epsilon_v)_{v\mid\infty}\in\F_2^r: \sum_v\epsilon_v=0\right\}. \] For the geometric neutral category of CM motives whose CM fields are subfields of $K$, with Betti functor as origin, this group classifies the isomorphism classes of rational fibre functors that become isomorphic to Betti at every finite completion. It has $2^{r-1}$ elements. Thus finite comparisons single out Betti only when $r=1$. Adding a real comparison singles it out for every $r$.
status: Proved
notes: All-places kernel is zero; finite-place kernel has 2^(r-1) elements.; Arithmetic Artin data and smaller subcategories require their actual group and cannot silently be replaced by S^K.; It is unique iff [K+:Q]=1; F=Q(sqrt5), K=F(i) gives the nontrivial class (-1,-1)_F.; Computed actual S^K cohomology, not merely the norm-one torus.

statement: Verified: a non-Betti form with all finite comparisons: Take $F=\Q(\sqrt5)$ and $K=F(i)$. The quaternion algebra $(-1,-1)_F$ is nonsplit at both real embeddings. It is split at every finite place: over $\Q$ Hamilton's algebra is ramified only at $2$ and infinity, and $2$ is inert in $F$ because $x^2-x-1$ is irreducible modulo two. The degree-two local extension at $2$ multiplies the invariant $1/2$ by two. The algebra is split by $K$, and its corestriction to $\Q$ is trivial since its two real invariants sum to zero in $\Q/\Z$. It is the nonzero element of $\Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K)\simeq\Z/2$. Equivalently, the corresponding $U$-torsor is $x^2+y^2=-1$ over $F$. Twisting Betti by its lift to an $S^K$-torsor supplies the asserted different rational fibre functor. The irreducibility calculation is recorded in the program.
status: Refuted; exact criterion proved
notes: It is unique iff [K+:Q]=1; F=Q(sqrt5), K=F(i) gives the nontrivial class (-1,-1)_F.; Computed actual S^K cohomology, not merely the norm-one torus.

statement: Proved: the complete lattice and rank answer to 15:151: The image $I_\Sigma$ of $\psi_\Sigma$ is the connected $\Q$-torus with character and cocharacter lattices \begin{align*} X^*(I_\Sigma)&=\Z^{I_E}/\ker(A^{\mathsf t}) \simeq\im(A^{\mathsf t})\subset\Z^{I_K},\\ X_*(I_\Sigma)&=(\im A\otimes\Q)\cap\Z^{I_E}. \end{align*} In particular $\dim I_\Sigma=\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)$. If $E$ is CM of degree $2g$, put \[ C_E=\{x\in\Res_{E/\Q}\Gm: x\overline x\in\Gm\subset\Res_{E^+/\Q}\Gm\}. \] Then $I_\Sigma\subset C_E$, and the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $I_\Sigma=C_E$; \item $\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)=g+1$; \item every rational row relation of $A$ is generated by $e_\sigma+e_{c\sigma}-e_\tau-e_{c\tau}$. \end{enumerate} These are effective necessary and sufficient conditions for every CM type, including non-Galois and imprimitive types. For the CM type $\Phi$ represented by $\Sigma$, $I_\Sigma=\MT(E,\Phi)$.

statement: Proved: the compact part in the manuscript's reduction: Let $V'_K=\ker(N_{K/\Q}:S^K\to\Gm)$, and let $\nu:C_E\to\Gm$ send $x$ to its common product $x_\sigma x_{c\sigma}$. Then \[ \psi_\Sigma(V'_K)=I_\Sigma\cap\ker\nu,\qquad \dim\psi_\Sigma(V'_K)=\operatorname{rank}_\Q A-1, \] and the character lattice of this image is \[ \im(A^{\mathsf t})/\Z\mathbf1_{I_K}. \] The image is all of the norm-one torus of $E/E^+$ precisely when $\operatorname{rank}_\Q A=g+1$.
